title.zh: 卷223 列傳十 万子：扈尔干 孟格布禄 扈尔干子岱善 孟格布禄子吴尔古代 杨吉砮兄清佳砮 杨吉砮子纳林布禄 金臺石 清佳砮子布寨 布寨子布扬古 布占泰 拜音达里
title.en: Volume 223 Biographies 10: Wan Son: Hu Er Gan, Meng Gebulu, Hu Er Gan Zi Dai Shan, Meng Ge Bu Lu Zi Wu Er Gu Dai, Yang Ji Nu Xiong Qing Jia Nu, Yang Ji Nu Zi Na Lin Bu Lu, Jin Taishi, Qing Jia Nu Zi Bu Zhai, Bu Zhai Zi Bu Yang Gu, Bu Zhan Tai, Bai Yin Da Li
title.raw: 卷223 列傳十 万子：扈尔干 孟格布禄 扈尔干子岱善 孟格布禄子吴尔古代 杨吉砮兄清佳砮 杨吉砮子纳林布禄 金臺石 清佳砮子布寨 布寨子布扬古 布占泰 拜音达里

sentences.zh: 萬楊吉砮布佔泰拜音達里

translations.literal: Wan, Yangginu, Butai, Bayindari.
translations.idiomatic: Biographies: Wan; Yangginu; Butai; Bayindari.

sentences.zh: 萬，哈達部長也。

translations.literal: Wan was the chieftain of the Hada tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Wan was chief of the Hada.

sentences.zh: 萬自稱汗，故謂之萬汗。

translations.literal: Wan styled himself khan, and so was called Khan Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Because he called himself khan, he was known as Khan Wan.

sentences.zh: 明譯爲王台，「台」「萬」音近。

translations.literal: The Ming rendered this as Wangtai, as the sounds of "tai" and "wan" are close.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming court transcribed his name as Wangtai, since tai and wan sound alike.

sentences.zh: 明於東邊酋長稱汗者，皆譯爲「王」某，若以王爲姓，萬亦其例也。

translations.literal: When eastern chiefs called themselves khan, the Ming all rendered them as "Wang" plus a name; if one takes Wang as a surname, Wan is also such a case.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming habitually rendered eastern chiefs who styled themselves khan as "Wang" followed by a personal name; read this way, Wan fits the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 哈達爲扈倫四部之一，明通稱海西。

translations.literal: Hada was one of the four Hūlun tribes, which the Ming commonly called Haixi collectively.
translations.idiomatic: Hada belonged to the four Hūlun tribes, known collectively to the Ming as the Haixi Jurchens.

sentences.zh: 哈達貢於明，入廣順關，地近南，故謂之南關。

translations.literal: Hada paid tribute to the Ming through Guangshun Pass; as its lands lay toward the south, it was called the Southern Pass faction.
translations.idiomatic: Because Hada paid tribute through Guangshun Pass and its territory lay far to the south, it was called the Southern Pass branch.

sentences.zh: 萬姓納喇氏，其始祖納齊卜祿。

translations.literal: Wan's clan was the Nara; his founding ancestor was Naqibolu.
translations.idiomatic: The Wan lineage was of the Nara clan, founded by Naqibolu.

sentences.zh: 納齊卜祿生尚延多爾和齊，尚延多爾和齊生嘉瑪喀碩珠古，嘉瑪喀碩珠古生綏屯，綏屯生都勒喜。

translations.literal: Naqibolu begat Shangyanduoerheqi; Shangyanduoerheqi begat Jiamakashuzhugu; Jiamakashuzhugu begat Suitun; Suitun begat Dulexi.
translations.idiomatic: Naqibolu was followed by Shangyanduoerheqi, then Jiamakashuzhugu, Suitun, and Dulexi in succession.

sentences.zh: 都勒喜子二：克什納、古對硃顏。

translations.literal: Dulexi had two sons: Keshina and Guduizhuyan.
translations.idiomatic: Dulexi had two sons, Keshina and Guduizhuyan.

sentences.zh: 古對硃顏之後別爲烏喇部。

translations.literal: Guduizhuyan's descendants separately became the Wula tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Guduizhuyan's line later split off as the Wula tribe.

sentences.zh: 克什納，嘉靖初掌塔山左衞，於諸部中最強，修貢謹，又捕叛者猛克有勞，明授左都督，賜金頂大帽；

translations.literal: Keshina, at the beginning of the Jiajing reign, held command of the Tashan Left Guard; among the tribes he was strongest, kept tribute carefully, and for capturing the rebel Mengke had merit; the Ming appointed him Left Military Commissioner and bestowed a golden-topped great cap;
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jiajing era Keshina commanded the Tashan Left Guard and was the strongest of the tribes; he maintained tribute scrupulously and earned merit by capturing the rebel Mengke, for which the Ming made him Left Military Commissioner and gave him a golden-topped great cap;

sentences.zh: 既，爲族人巴代達爾漢所殺。

translations.literal: Afterward he was killed by his tribesman Badai Daerhan.
translations.idiomatic: He was later killed by his kinsman Badai Daerhan.

sentences.zh: 克什納子二：長徹徹穆，次旺濟外蘭。

translations.literal: Keshina had two sons: the eldest Chechemu, the second Wangji Wailan.
translations.idiomatic: Keshina had two sons: the elder Chechemu and the younger Wangji Wailan.

sentences.zh: 克什納死時，徹徹穆子萬奔席北部境綏哈城，而旺濟外蘭奔哈達，遂爲其部長。

translations.literal: When Keshina died, Chechemu's son Wan fled north of the border to Suiha City in the Xibu region, while Wangji Wailan fled to Hada and became chieftain of that tribe.
translations.idiomatic: At Keshina's death Chechemu's son Wan fled beyond the border to Suiha City in the northern Xibu lands, while Wangji Wailan took refuge in Hada and became its chieftain.

sentences.zh: 明以其偵寇功，授都督僉事。

translations.literal: The Ming, for his merit in scouting bandits, appointed him Vice Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming rewarded his service in scouting raiders with the post of Vice Military Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 葉赫部長褚孔格數爲亂，旺濟外蘭執而僇之，奪其貢敕七百道，及所部十三寨。

translations.literal: The Yehhe chieftain Zhukongge repeatedly caused disturbances; Wangji Wailan seized and executed him, taking seven hundred tribute patents and thirteen of his stockaded villages.
translations.idiomatic: The Yehhe chief Zhukongge had stirred up trouble more than once; Wangji Wailan seized and put him to death, taking seven hundred tribute patents and thirteen of his stockaded villages.

sentences.zh: 後其部衆叛，旺濟外蘭爲所殺。

translations.literal: Later his tribesmen rebelled and Wangji Wailan was killed by them.
translations.idiomatic: His followers later rebelled, and Wangji Wailan was killed in the uprising.

sentences.zh: 其子博爾坤舍進殺父仇，迎從兄萬於綏哈城，還長其部。

translations.literal: His son Bo'erkun Shejin killed his father's enemy and welcomed his cousin Wan from Suiha City back to lead the tribe.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bo'erkun Shejin avenged his father, brought his cousin Wan back from Suiha City, and restored him as tribal chief.

sentences.zh: 萬能用其衆，略隣部，遠交而近攻，勢益盛，遂以哈達爲國，稱汗。

translations.literal: Wan was able to employ his followers, raided neighboring tribes, made distant alliances and attacked nearby ones; his power grew ever greater, and he made Hada a state and styled himself khan.
translations.idiomatic: Wan knew how to wield his followers: he raided neighboring tribes, befriended the distant and struck the near, and his power swelled until he made Hada a realm and took the title of khan.

sentences.zh: 興祖諸子環居赫圖阿喇，號「寧古塔貝勒」，與董鄂部搆釁。

translations.literal: The sons of Xingzu dwelled around Hetu Ala, styled "Ningguta beile," and feuded with the Dong'e tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzu's sons settled around Hetu Ala as the "Ningguta beile" and came into conflict with the Dong'e tribe.

sentences.zh: 興祖第三子索長阿爲其子吳泰娶萬女，蓋嘗乞兵於萬以禦董鄂部。

translations.literal: Xingzu's third son Suochanga married his son Wu Tai to Wan's daughter, having once begged troops from Wan to resist the Dong'e tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzu's third son Suochanga had his son Wu Tai marry Wan's daughter, for he had once sought Wan's troops against the Dong'e.

sentences.zh: 萬居靜安堡外，室廬、耕植與他部落異，事明謹。

translations.literal: Wan dwelled outside Jing'an Fort; his dwellings, farming, and planting differed from other tribes, and he served the Ming scrupulously.
translations.idiomatic: Wan lived beyond Jing'an Fort, where his houses and farming differed from other tribes; he served the Ming with scrupulous loyalty.

sentences.zh: 是時王杲領建州，與韃靼東西遙應，窺遼塞，萬支拄其間不令合。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Gao led Jianzhou and coordinated with the Tatars east and west, eyeing the Liaodong border; Wan propped himself between them and did not let them unite.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Gao led Jianzhou and coordinated with the Tatars east and west to probe the Liaodong frontier; Wan stood between them and kept the two sides from joining forces.

sentences.zh: 明使繼其大父克什納爲都督。

translations.literal: The Ming continued his great-grandfather Keshina as Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming confirmed him in his great-grandfather Keshina's post of Military Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 王杲盜邊，開原兵備副使王之弼檄萬，令王杲還所掠。

translations.literal: Wang Gao raided the border; the Kaiyuan circuit military vice commissioner Wang Zhibi dispatched Wan to have Wang Gao return what he had plundered.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Gao raided the frontier, the Kaiyuan circuit vice commissioner Wang Zhibi ordered Wan to make Wang Gao restore what he had taken.

sentences.zh: 萬入建州寨，要王杲盟於撫順關下，復通市如故。

translations.literal: Wan entered the Jianzhou stockade and required Wang Gao to covenant at Fushun Pass, restoring markets as before.
translations.idiomatic: Wan entered the Jianzhou stockade and compelled Wang Gao to swear an oath beneath Fushun Pass, after which trade resumed as before.

sentences.zh: 土默特徙帳遼東，萬入貢，多奪其馬。

translations.literal: Tümed shifted their camp to Liaodong; Wan went to present tribute and often seized their horses.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tümed shifted their camp into Liaodong, Wan came to pay tribute and often seized their horses.

sentences.zh: 已而，土默特弟韋徵與萬爲婚，其從子小黃台吉擁五萬騎，介葉赫復請婚於萬，萬懼而許之。

translations.literal: Later Tümed's younger brother Wei Zheng made marriage with Wan; his nephew the Little Yellow Taiji, with fifty thousand horsemen, interposed through Yehhe and again requested marriage with Wan; Wan feared this and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Tümed's younger brother Wei Zheng allied with Wan by marriage; his nephew the Little Yellow Taiji, commanding fifty thousand horsemen and passing through Yehhe, again sought Wan's daughter in marriage, and Wan, afraid, consented.

sentences.zh: 小黃台吉以馬牛羊、甲胄、貂豹之裘遺萬，築壇刑白馬爲盟，約毋犯塞。

translations.literal: The Little Yellow Taiji presented Wan with horses, cattle, sheep, armor, and sable-marten pelts; they built an altar and slew a white horse in alliance, covenanting not to violate the border.
translations.idiomatic: The Little Yellow Taiji sent Wan horses, cattle, sheep, armor, and sable and leopard furs; they built an altar, sacrificed a white horse, and pledged not to raid the frontier.

sentences.zh: 居無何，小黃台吉要萬犯塞，萬不可，乃罷，時爲萬曆元年。

translations.literal: Before long, the Little Yellow Taiji wanted Wan to violate the border; Wan refused, and the matter ended—this was the first year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Little Yellow Taiji pressed Wan to raid the frontier; Wan refused and the plan came to nothing. This was the first year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 明年，王杲亂，遼東巡撫張學顏檄萬捕王杲。

translations.literal: The next year Wang Gao rebelled; the Liaodong circuit censor Zhang Xueyan dispatched Wan to capture Wang Gao.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Wang Gao rose in revolt, and the Liaodong censor Zhang Xueyan ordered Wan to seize him.

sentences.zh: 萬令海西、建州諸酋款塞，乞先開市，游擊丁倣語之曰：「必得王杲而後市可圖也。」

translations.literal: Wan ordered the Haixi and Jianzhou chiefs to present themselves at the pass and beg to open markets first; the patrol officer Ding Fang told them: "Only after Wang Gao is taken can markets be considered."
translations.idiomatic: Wan had the Haixi and Jianzhou chiefs come to the pass and plead for markets to open first; the patrol officer Ding Fang told them, "Markets can be discussed only after Wang Gao is taken."

sentences.zh: 萬復率建州衞都督大疼克等叩關，督撫以聞，許開市，遂縛獻王杲所掠遼軍八十四人，及種人兀黑，以兀黑嘗殺漢官也。

translations.literal: Wan again led Jianzhou guard military commissioner Da Tengke and others to knock at the pass; the governor and censor reported upward, and permission to open markets was granted; they then bound and presented eighty-four Liaodong troops plundered by Wang Gao and the tribesman Wu Hei—because Wu Hei had once killed a Han official.
translations.idiomatic: Wan again led the Jianzhou guard commissioner Da Tengke and others to the pass; the governor and censor reported up, markets were allowed to open, and they delivered bound eighty-four Liaodong soldiers Wang Gao had seized, together with the tribesman Wu Hei, who had once killed a Han official.

sentences.zh: 又明年，捕得王杲，檻致京師。

translations.literal: The year after that, they captured Wang Gao and sent him caged to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that Wang Gao was captured and sent to the capital in a cage.

sentences.zh: 明進萬右柱國、龍虎將軍，官二子都督僉事，賜黃金二十兩、大紅師子紵衣一襲。

translations.literal: The Ming advanced Wan to Right Pillar of State and Dragon-Tiger General, made two sons Vice Military Commissioners, and bestowed twenty taels of gold and one great red lion-pattern robe.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming promoted Wan to Right Pillar of State and Dragon-Tiger General, appointed two of his sons Vice Military Commissioners, and gave him twenty taels of gold and a great red lion-pattern robe.

sentences.zh: 是時萬所領地，東則輝發、烏喇，南則建州，北則葉赫，延袤千里，保塞甚盛。

translations.literal: At this time the territory Wan ruled extended east to Huifa and Wula, south to Jianzhou, north to Yehhe—a thousand li in extent—with very strong border defenses.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Wan's domain stretched a thousand li from Huifa and Wula in the east to Jianzhou in the south and Yehhe in the north, and his border defenses were formidable.

sentences.zh: 萬暴而黷貨，以事赴訴，視賂有無爲曲直。

translations.literal: Wan was brutal and greedy for goods; when parties came to lodge suits, he judged right and wrong by whether gifts were offered.
translations.idiomatic: Wan was violent and greedy; when people brought suits before him, he judged right and wrong by whether they paid him.

sentences.zh: 部下皆效之，使於諸部，驕恣無所忌，求賄鷹、犬、雞、豚惟所欲。

translations.literal: His subordinates all imitated him; when sent to other tribes they were arrogant and unrestrained, demanding hawks, dogs, chickens, and pigs as they wished.
translations.idiomatic: His followers copied him; when sent among the tribes they were arrogant and unrestrained, demanding hawks, dogs, chickens, and pigs at will.

sentences.zh: 使還，意爲毀譽，萬輒信之。

translations.literal: When the envoys returned, whatever praise or blame they gave, Wan believed it at once.
translations.idiomatic: When his envoys returned, whatever praise or blame they offered, Wan believed it at once.

sentences.zh: 以是諸部皆貳。

translations.literal: For this reason all the tribes turned disloyal.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this every tribe turned against him.

sentences.zh: 而葉赫部長清佳砮、楊吉砮兄弟，以父褚孔格見僇，心怨萬。

translations.literal: Yet the Yehhe chiefs Qingjianu and Yangginu, brothers, resented Wan because their father Zhukongge had been executed.
translations.idiomatic: The Yehhe brothers Qingjianu and Yangginu, however, bore Wan a grudge because their father Zhukongge had been put to death.

sentences.zh: 萬納其女弟溫姐，又以女妻楊吉砮，卵翼之。

translations.literal: Wan took Qingjianu's younger sister Wenjie in marriage and also gave a daughter in marriage to Yangginu, cherishing them.
translations.idiomatic: Wan took Qingjianu's younger sister Wenjie as wife and gave another daughter to Yangginu, sheltering them both.

sentences.zh: 萬老而衰，楊吉砮復婚於哈屯恍惚太，勢漸張。

translations.literal: Wan grew old and feeble; Yangginu again married into the Haton Huanghu Tai clan and his power gradually expanded.
translations.idiomatic: As Wan aged and weakened, Yangginu married again into the Haton Huanghu Tai clan, and his power steadily grew.

sentences.zh: 萬子扈爾干尤暴，所部或去從楊吉砮。

translations.literal: Wan's son Huergan was especially brutal; some of his followers left to join Yangginu.
translations.idiomatic: Wan's son Huergan was especially brutal, and some of his followers deserted to Yangginu.

sentences.zh: 楊吉砮搆烏喇與扈爾干爲仇，遂收故所部諸寨爲旺濟外蘭所侵者，取其八寨，惟把太等五寨尚屬萬。

translations.literal: Yangginu incited Wula and Huergan into enmity, then recovered the stockaded villages once seized by Wangji Wailan, taking eight of them; only Batai and five other villages still belonged to Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Yangginu set Wula and Huergan at odds, then recovered the stockades Wangji Wailan had seized, taking eight of them; only Batai and five other villages still remained Wan's.

sentences.zh: 自是輝發、烏喇諸部皆不受約束，萬地日蹙，憂憤不自憀。

translations.literal: From then on the Huifa and Wula tribes all ceased to accept restraint; Wan's territory shrank daily, and he was anguished and wretched.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Huifa, Wula, and the other tribes no longer submitted to his authority; Wan's lands shrank day by day, and he sank into grief and despair.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十年七月，萬卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the tenth year of Wanli, Wan died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the tenth year of Wanli, Wan died.

sentences.zh: 葉赫聞萬死，使求故貢敕，扈爾干曰：「我父以汝兄弟故，卒用憂憤死，今尚問敕書乎？」

translations.literal: When Yehhe heard Wan had died, they sent to demand the old tribute patents; Huergan said: "My father died of worry and rage because of you brothers—do you still ask for the patents?"
translations.idiomatic: When Yehhe heard of Wan's death, they sent to demand the old tribute patents. Huergan said, "My father died of grief and rage because of you brothers—do you still ask for the patents?"

sentences.zh: 勿與，告哀於明。

translations.literal: He would not give them and appealed in grief to the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: He refused and appealed in grief to the Ming.

sentences.zh: 明以萬忠，賜祭，予採幣、四表裏。

translations.literal: The Ming, considering Wan loyal, bestowed funeral rites and gave sacrificial silks and four suits each of inner and outer garments.
translations.idiomatic: Honoring Wan's loyalty, the Ming sent funeral offerings and gave sacrificial silks and four suits of inner and outer garments.

sentences.zh: 萬有子五：扈爾干爲長；

translations.literal: Wan had five sons: the eldest was Huergan;
translations.idiomatic: Wan had five sons. The eldest was Huergan;

sentences.zh: 仲、叔皆前死；

translations.literal: the second and third had died earlier;
translations.idiomatic: the second and third had died before him;

sentences.zh: 季孟格布祿，溫姐子也；

translations.literal: the fourth was Menggebulu, son of Wenjie;
translations.idiomatic: the fourth was Menggebulu, Wenjie's son;

sentences.zh: 又有康古魯，爲萬外婦子。

translations.literal: and there was also Kanguru, son of Wan's concubine.
translations.idiomatic: there was also Kanguru, born to Wan's concubine.

sentences.zh: 萬卒，康古魯與扈爾干爭父業。

translations.literal: When Wan died, Kanguru and Huergan contended for their father's estate.
translations.idiomatic: When Wan died, Kanguru and Huergan fought over their father's inheritance.

sentences.zh: 扈爾干怒曰：「汝，我父外婦子也，寧得爭父業乎？

translations.literal: Huergan angrily said: "You are my father's son by a concubine—how can you contend for his estate?
translations.idiomatic: Huergan raged, "You are my father's son by a concubine—how dare you claim his estate?

sentences.zh: 不避我，我且殺汝！」

translations.literal: If you do not avoid me, I shall kill you!"
translations.idiomatic: If you do not get out of my way, I will kill you!"

sentences.zh: 康古魯因亡抵清佳砮，清佳砮妻以女。

translations.literal: Kanguru therefore fled to Qingjianu, who gave him a daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Kanguru fled to Qingjianu, who gave him a daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 是時太祖初起兵。

translations.literal: At this time the Taizu had just begun to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the Taizu had only just begun to raise his army.

sentences.zh: 八月，扈爾干以兵從兆佳城長李岱劫太祖所屬瑚濟寨，太祖部將安費揚古、巴遜以十二人追擊，殺哈達兵四十人，還所掠。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Huergan with troops followed the chief of Zhaojia City, Li Dai, in raiding Huji stockade belonging to the Taizu; the Taizu's generals Anfiyanggu and Baxun pursued with twelve men, killed forty Hada soldiers, and recovered what had been plundered.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Huergan joined the chief of Zhaojia City, Li Dai, in raiding the Taizu's Huji stockade; the Taizu's generals Anfiyanggu and Baxun pursued with twelve men, killed forty Hada soldiers, and recovered the plunder.

sentences.zh: 扈爾干旋卒。

translations.literal: Huergan soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Huergan soon died.

sentences.zh: 孟格布祿年十九，襲父職龍虎將軍、左都督，衆未附。

translations.literal: Menggebulu, nineteen years old, inherited his father's posts of Dragon-Tiger General and Left Military Commissioner; the tribesmen were not yet attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: Menggebulu, nineteen years old, inherited his father's titles of Dragon-Tiger General and Left Military Commissioner, but the tribes had not yet rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 康古魯聞扈爾干死，遂還，烝溫姐。

translations.literal: When Kanguru heard Huergan had died, he returned and took Wenjie as wife in the levirate.
translations.idiomatic: When Kanguru heard Huergan was dead, he returned and took Wenjie to wife by levirate.

sentences.zh: 扈爾干有子曰岱善，與康古魯、孟格布祿析萬遺業爲三。

translations.literal: Huergan had a son named Daishan, who with Kanguru and Menggebulu divided Wan's legacy into three.
translations.idiomatic: Huergan had a son Daishan, who with Kanguru and Menggebulu divided Wan's estate three ways.

sentences.zh: 康古魯報扈爾干之怨，釋憾於其子；

translations.literal: Kanguru, to repay his grudge against Huergan, let go his enmity toward Huergan's son;
translations.idiomatic: Kanguru, to settle his score with Huergan, set aside his hatred of Huergan's son;

sentences.zh: 孟格布祿亦以母溫姐故，助康古魯，共攻岱善；

translations.literal: Menggebulu also, because of his mother Wenjie, helped Kanguru in jointly attacking Daishan;
translations.idiomatic: Menggebulu also, for his mother Wenjie's sake, aided Kanguru in attacking Daishan together;

sentences.zh: 而清佳砮、楊吉砮兄弟謀攻萬子孫報仇，十一年七月，挾煖兔、恍惚太等萬騎來攻。

translations.literal: while the brothers Qingjianu and Yangginu of Yehhe plotted to attack Wan's descendants for revenge—in the seventh month of the eleventh year they came to attack with ten thousand horsemen led by Nuantu, Huanghu Tai, and others.
translations.idiomatic: while the brothers Qingjianu and Yangginu of Yehhe plotted revenge against Wan's descendants; in the seventh month of the eleventh year they attacked with ten thousand horsemen under Nuantu, Huanghu Tai, and others.

sentences.zh: 明總督侍郎周詠念岱善弱，孟格布祿少，請加敕部諸酋，神宗許之。

translations.literal: The Ming grand coordinator Zhou Yong, seeing Daishan weak and Menggebulu young, requested additional patents for the tribal chiefs; the Shenzong Emperor granted this.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming grand coordinator Zhou Yong, seeing Daishan weak and Menggebulu young, asked that additional patents be issued to the tribal chiefs, and the Shenzong Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 十二月，楊吉砮等復挾蒙古科爾沁貝勒瓮阿岱等萬騎來攻，孟格布祿及岱善以二千騎迎戰而敗。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Yangginu and others again came to attack with ten thousand horsemen including the Mongol Horqin prince Weng Adai; Menggebulu and Daishan met them with two thousand horsemen and were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Yangginu again attacked with ten thousand horsemen, including the Mongol Horqin prince Weng Adai; Menggebulu and Daishan met them with two thousand horsemen and were defeated.

sentences.zh: 自是兵屢至，恣焚掠不已。

translations.literal: From then on troops came repeatedly, burning and plundering without cease.
translations.idiomatic: From then on their armies came again and again, burning and plundering without end.

sentences.zh: 十二年，明總兵李成梁誘殺清佳砮、楊吉砮兄弟，所部讋服，誓受孟格布祿約束。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, the Ming commander Li Chenglang lured and killed the brothers Qingjianu and Yangginu; their followers were cowed into submission and swore to accept Menggebulu's authority.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the Ming commander Li Chenglang lured and killed the brothers Qingjianu and Yangginu; their followers submitted in fear and swore to obey Menggebulu.

sentences.zh: 葉赫難始紓，而內訌復急。

translations.literal: The Yehhe crisis began to ease, yet internal strife flared again.
translations.idiomatic: The Yehhe threat began to ease, but internal strife flared anew.

sentences.zh: 清佳砮子布寨、楊吉砮子納林布祿乘隙圖報怨。

translations.literal: Qingjianu's son Buzhai and Yangginu's son Nalinbulu seized the opportunity to plan revenge.
translations.idiomatic: Qingjianu's son Buzhai and Yangginu's son Nalinbulu seized the chance to plot revenge.

sentences.zh: 十五年四月，納林布祿以恍惚太萬騎攻把泰寨，明兵來援，圍解；

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifteenth year, Nalinbulu attacked Batai stockade with ten thousand horsemen of Huanghu Tai; Ming troops came to relieve the siege and it was lifted;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fifteenth year Nalinbulu attacked Batai stockade with ten thousand horsemen of Huanghu Tai; Ming troops came to the rescue and the siege was lifted;

sentences.zh: 乃陰結其姑溫姐，嗾孟格布祿佐康古魯圖岱善。

translations.literal: then he secretly joined his aunt Wenjie and incited Menggebulu to assist Kanguru in plotting against Daishan.
translations.idiomatic: then he secretly won over his aunt Wenjie and urged Menggebulu to help Kanguru plot against Daishan.

sentences.zh: 先是扈爾干許以女歸太祖，十六年，岱善親送以往，太祖爲設宴成禮。

translations.literal: Previously Huergan had promised a daughter to the Taizu; in the sixteenth year Daishan personally escorted her there, and the Taizu held a feast to complete the marriage rites.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Huergan had promised a daughter to the Taizu; in the sixteenth year Daishan escorted her there in person, and the Taizu held a feast to complete the marriage.

sentences.zh: 是年納林布祿復以恍惚太五千騎圍岱善。

translations.literal: That year Nalinbulu again besieged Daishan with five thousand horsemen of Huanghu Tai.
translations.idiomatic: That year Nalinbulu again besieged Daishan with five thousand horsemen of Huanghu Tai.

sentences.zh: 孟格布祿將其孥從納林布祿往葉赫，居十八里寨，於是圖岱善益急，而康古魯誘岱善所部叛岱善，略其貲畜，納林布祿並掠岱善妻哈爾屯以去。

translations.literal: Menggebulu led his wives and children to follow Nalinbulu to Yehhe, residing at the Eighteen-li stockade; the plot against Daishan grew more urgent; Kanguru enticed Daishan's followers to rebel, plundered his wealth and livestock, and Nalinbulu also seized Daishan's wife Hartun and took her away.
translations.idiomatic: Menggebulu took his family to Yehhe with Nalinbulu and lived at the Eighteen-li stockade; the plot against Daishan grew fiercer; Kanguru turned Daishan's followers against him and seized his goods and livestock, and Nalinbulu carried off Daishan's wife Hartun.

sentences.zh: 明邊吏議絕孟格布祿市，以所部及土田、牲畜盡歸於岱善。

translations.literal: Ming border officials discussed cutting off markets to Menggebulu and assigning all his followers, lands, and livestock to Daishan.
translations.idiomatic: Ming border officials proposed cutting off trade with Menggebulu and assigning all his followers, lands, and livestock to Daishan.

sentences.zh: 孟格布祿不聽，復與布寨、納林布祿、康古魯入開原，溫姐偕。

translations.literal: Menggebulu would not listen and again entered Kaiyuan with Buzhai, Nalinbulu, and Kanguru—Wenjie accompanying them.
translations.idiomatic: Menggebulu refused and again entered Kaiyuan with Buzhai, Nalinbulu, and Kanguru, Wenjie with them.

sentences.zh: 開原兵備副使王緘令裨將襲其營，執溫姐、康古魯以歸。

translations.literal: The Kaiyuan circuit military vice commissioner Wang Jian ordered a subordinate general to raid their camp and captured Wenjie and Kanguru.
translations.idiomatic: The Kaiyuan circuit vice commissioner Wang Jian ordered a subordinate to raid their camp and brought back Wenjie and Kanguru as prisoners.

sentences.zh: 巡撫顧養謙諭孟格布祿：「和岱善，還所掠，否則斷若母頭矣！」

translations.literal: The circuit censor Gu Yangqian instructed Menggebulu: "Make peace with Daishan and return what you plundered, or I shall cut off your mother's head!"
translations.idiomatic: The censor Gu Yangqian warned Menggebulu, "Make peace with Daishan and return what you took, or I will cut off your mother's head!"

sentences.zh: 王緘以爲戮溫姐則孟​​格布祿益攜，不如釋之，而囚康古魯，待朝命。

translations.literal: Wang Jian held that killing Wenjie would alienate Menggebulu further; it were better to release her and imprison Kanguru, awaiting the court's command.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian argued that executing Wenjie would only drive Menggebulu further away; it were better to release her and hold Kanguru until the court decided.

sentences.zh: 溫姐既得脫，遁還。

translations.literal: Once Wenjie had escaped, she fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wenjie had escaped, she fled home.

sentences.zh: 孟格布祿自葉赫攻岱善，自焚其所居，劫溫姐去。

translations.literal: Menggebulu attacked Daishan from Yehhe, burned his own residence, and seized Wenjie away.
translations.idiomatic: Menggebulu attacked Daishan from Yehhe, burned his own dwelling, and carried Wenjie off by force.

sentences.zh: 王緘坐是奪職。

translations.literal: Wang Jian was demoted for this.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian lost his post over the affair.

sentences.zh: 十六年二月，河西大饑，岱善乞糴於明，明予粟百斛。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixteenth year, a great famine struck west of the river; Daishan begged grain from the Ming, who gave him a hundred hu of millet.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixteenth year a great famine struck west of the river; Daishan begged grain from the Ming, who gave him a hundred hu of millet.

sentences.zh: 李成梁出師討布寨、孟格布祿，圍其城，布寨、孟格布祿請降，成梁振旅還。

translations.literal: Li Chenglang marched out to punish Buzhai and Menggebulu, besieged their city; Buzhai and Menggebulu requested surrender, and Chenglang withdrew his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chenglang marched against Buzhai and Menggebulu and besieged their city; they sued for peace, and Chenglang withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 開原兵備副使成遜議釋康古魯，和諸部；

translations.literal: The Kaiyuan circuit military vice commissioner Cheng Xun proposed releasing Kanguru to reconcile the tribes;
translations.idiomatic: The Kaiyuan circuit vice commissioner Cheng Xun proposed releasing Kanguru to reconcile the tribes;

sentences.zh: 總督侍郎顧養謙亦謂：「岱善弱而多疑，即殲諸酋立之，不能有其衆。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Gu Yangqian also said: "Daishan is weak and suspicious; even if the other chiefs were destroyed and he were set up, he could not hold his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Gu Yangqian also said, "Daishan is weak and suspicious; even if we destroyed the other chiefs and set him up, he could not hold his people.

sentences.zh: 不如釋康古魯，使和岱善，則萬子孫皆全。

translations.literal: Better to release Kanguru and have him reconcile with Daishan, so that all of Wan's descendants may be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Better to release Kanguru and have him reconcile with Daishan, so that all of Wan's line may survive.

sentences.zh: 岱善內倚中國，外結建州，陰折北關謀，實制東陲勝策也。」

translations.literal: With Daishan relying inward on China and outward allying with Jianzhou, secretly checking Northern Pass intrigues—this is in truth the superior strategy for controlling the eastern frontier."
translations.idiomatic: With Daishan leaning on China within and allying with Jianzhou without, secretly checking Northern Pass designs—this is truly the best way to control the eastern frontier."

sentences.zh: 夏四月，遂釋康古魯而諭之曰：「中國立岱善，以萬故；

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, Kanguru was released and admonished: "China established Daishan for Wan's sake;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer Kanguru was released and told, "China established Daishan for Wan's sake;

sentences.zh: 囚汝，以助北關侵岱善也。

translations.literal: you were imprisoned for aiding the Northern Pass in encroaching on Daishan.
translations.idiomatic: you were imprisoned for helping the Northern Pass encroach on Daishan.

sentences.zh: 汝亦萬子，不忍殺。

translations.literal: You too are Wan's son—we could not bear to kill you.
translations.idiomatic: You too are Wan's son, and we could not bear to kill you.

sentences.zh: 今釋汝，和諸酋，修父業。

translations.literal: Now you are released—reconcile with the chiefs and restore your father's enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Now you are released: reconcile with the chiefs and restore your father's estate.

sentences.zh: 岱善安危，汝則任之。」

translations.literal: Daishan's safety is your responsibility."
translations.idiomatic: Daishan's safety rests on you."

sentences.zh: 康古魯聽命，因令岱善以叔父事康古魯，以祖母事溫姐，刑牲盟；

translations.literal: Kanguru obeyed; Daishan was made to treat Kanguru as uncle and Wenjie as grandmother, and they slaughtered animals in covenant;
translations.idiomatic: Kanguru obeyed; Daishan was made to treat Kanguru as uncle and Wenjie as grandmother, and they sacrificed animals in alliance;

sentences.zh: 且進布寨、納林布祿使者誡諭之，爲均兩部，敕孟格布祿出岱善妻子五人，及所部種人三百二十三、婦稚五百四十三、馬牛羊數百，歸岱善。

translations.literal: and he sent envoys from Buzhai and Nalinbulu to warn them, balancing the two factions; Menggebulu was ordered to return Daishan's five wives and children and three hundred twenty-three tribespeople, five hundred forty-three women and children, and hundreds of horses, cattle, and sheep to Daishan.
translations.idiomatic: and he sent envoys from Buzhai and Nalinbulu to warn them and balance the two sides; Menggebulu was ordered to return Daishan's five wives and children, three hundred twenty-three tribesmen, five hundred forty-three women and children, and hundreds of horses, cattle, and sheep.

sentences.zh: 康古魯偕溫姐歸故寨，居月餘，康古魯病且死，語溫姐及孟格布祿，戒部曲毋盜邊負明恩。

translations.literal: Kanguru returned with Wenjie to the old stockade; after more than a month Kanguru fell ill and near death, telling Wenjie and Menggebulu, admonishing his followers not to raid the border and betray Ming favor.
translations.idiomatic: Kanguru returned with Wenjie to their old stockade; after a month he fell mortally ill and told Wenjie and Menggebulu to forbid their followers from raiding the frontier and betraying Ming favor.

sentences.zh: 康古魯死，孟格布祿謀盡室徙依葉赫，度溫姐不從，微告布寨、納林布祿以兵至。

translations.literal: When Kanguru died, Menggebulu planned to move his entire household to rely on Yehhe; knowing Wenjie would not consent, he secretly told Buzhai and Nalinbulu to bring troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Kanguru died, Menggebulu planned to move his whole household to Yehhe; knowing Wenjie would refuse, he secretly summoned Buzhai and Nalinbulu with troops.

sentences.zh: 孟格布祿縱火燔其居，趣溫姐行，溫姐不可，强扶持上馬，鬱鬱不自得，七月亦死。

translations.literal: Menggebulu set fire and burned his dwelling, urged Wenjie to go; Wenjie would not, was forcibly helped onto a horse, depressed and ill at ease, and in the seventh month also died.
translations.idiomatic: Menggebulu burned his dwelling and pressed Wenjie to leave; she refused, was forced onto a horse, sank into gloom, and died in the seventh month as well.

sentences.zh: 布寨、納林布祿誘孟格布祿圖岱善如故。

translations.literal: Buzhai and Nalinbulu incited Menggebulu to plot against Daishan as before.
translations.idiomatic: Buzhai and Nalinbulu again incited Menggebulu to plot against Daishan.

sentences.zh: 成遜令諸酋面相要釋憾，併入貢，而太祖日强盛，布寨、納林布祿與有隙。

translations.literal: Cheng Xun ordered the chiefs to meet face to face to release enmity and pay tribute jointly; but the Taizu grew stronger daily, and Buzhai and Nalinbulu had a grudge against him.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xun had the chiefs meet face to face to bury their grudges and pay joint tribute, but the Taizu grew stronger by the day, and Buzhai and Nalinbulu bore him a grudge.

sentences.zh: 二十一年夏六月，糾孟格布祿及烏喇、輝發四部合兵攻太祖，略戶布察寨。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of summer of the twenty-first year, they joined Menggebulu and the four tribes of Wula and Huifa in attacking the Taizu, raiding Hubucha stockade.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer of the twenty-first year they joined Menggebulu and the four tribes of Wula and Huifa to attack the Taizu and raided Hubucha stockade.

sentences.zh: 太祖率兵追之，設伏於中途，引兵略哈達富兒家齊寨。

translations.literal: The Taizu led troops in pursuit, set ambushes on the way, and led troops to raid the Hada stockade of Fu'erjiaqi.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu pursued with his army, laid ambushes along the route, and led a detachment to raid the Hada stockade of Fu'erjiaqi.

sentences.zh: 哈達兵至，太祖欲引敵至設伏所揮衆使退，以單騎殿。

translations.literal: When Hada troops arrived, the Taizu wished to lure the enemy to the ambush point and ordered his troops to withdraw, acting as rearguard alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: When Hada troops arrived, the Taizu meant to draw them to the ambush, ordered his men to withdraw, and rode alone as rearguard.

sentences.zh: 孟格布祿以三騎自後相迫，一騎出於前，太祖引弓射前騎，前騎在右，回身自馬項上發矢，矢著於馬腹，遂逸去。

translations.literal: Menggebulu with three horsemen pressed from behind; one horseman came from the front; the Taizu drew his bow and shot the front rider; the front rider was on the right and turned from the horse's neck to shoot; the arrow struck the horse's belly and he fled.
translations.idiomatic: Menggebulu pressed him with three horsemen from behind while one closed from the front; the Taizu shot the foremost rider, who wheeled from the horse's neck to return fire; the arrow struck his mount's belly and he fled.

sentences.zh: 三騎驟至，太祖馬驚幾墜，右足絓於鞍，復乘，遂射孟格布祿馬踣地，其從者秦穆布祿授以己馬，挾以馳。

translations.literal: The three horsemen suddenly arrived; the Taizu's horse startled and nearly threw him; his right foot caught in the saddle; he mounted again and shot Menggebulu's horse to the ground; his follower Qin Mubulu gave him his own horse and carried him off at a gallop.
translations.idiomatic: The three horsemen closed in; the Taizu's mount shied and nearly threw him, his right foot caught in the stirrup; he remounted, shot Menggebulu's horse down, and his follower Qin Mubulu gave him his own horse and bore him away at a gallop.

sentences.zh: 太祖率所部兵騎者三、步者二十，逐而擊之，斬十二人，獲甲六、馬十八，以還。

translations.literal: The Taizu with three cavalry and twenty infantry of his command pursued and struck them, beheading twelve men, capturing six suits of armor and eighteen horses, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu pursued with three horsemen and twenty foot soldiers, killed twelve men, took six suits of armor and eighteen horses, and returned.

sentences.zh: 九月，復從布寨、納林布祿以九部之兵三萬人攻太祖，戰於黑濟格城下，九部之兵熸，布寨殲焉。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, again with Buzhai and Nalinbulu they attacked the Taizu with thirty thousand men from nine tribes; they fought below Heijige City; the nine tribes' troops were extinguished and Buzhai was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Buzhai and Nalinbulu again attacked the Taizu with thirty thousand men from nine tribes at Heijige City; the allied army was shattered and Buzhai was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，葉赫諸部請成於太祖，盟定輒背之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, the Yehhe tribes asked peace with the Taizu, but whenever they covenanted they broke it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year the Yehhe tribes sued for peace with the Taizu, yet broke every covenant they made.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，孟格布祿所居城北溪流血。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, the stream north of Menggebulu's city ran with blood.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year the stream north of Menggebulu's city ran with blood.

sentences.zh: 二十七年秋，納林布祿攻孟格布祿，孟格布祿不能支，以其三子質於太祖，乞師。

translations.literal: In autumn of the twenty-seventh year, Nalinbulu attacked Menggebulu; Menggebulu could not hold out and sent his three sons as hostages to the Taizu, begging troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the twenty-seventh year Nalinbulu attacked Menggebulu, who could not hold out and sent his three sons as hostages to the Taizu to beg for troops.

sentences.zh: 太祖使費英東、噶蓋以兵二千戍哈達。

translations.literal: The Taizu sent Fei Yingdong and Gagai with two thousand troops to garrison Hada.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu sent Fei Yingdong and Gagai with two thousand men to garrison Hada.

sentences.zh: 納林布祿恐，乃搆明開原譯者爲書，誘孟格布祿使貳於明，將襲擊費英東等。

translations.literal: Nalinbulu feared this and had Ming Kaiyuan translators write letters inciting Menggebulu to turn against the Ming, planning to strike Fei Yingdong and others.
translations.idiomatic: Nalinbulu, afraid, had Ming translators at Kaiyuan write letters to turn Menggebulu against the Ming and planned to strike Fei Yingdong and his men.

sentences.zh: 費英東等詗得之，以告太祖。

translations.literal: Fei Yingdong and others learned of it by espionage and reported to the Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yingdong learned of the plot through espionage and reported it to the Taizu.

sentences.zh: 九月丁未朔，太祖帥師攻哈達。

translations.literal: On the first day of the ninth month, dingwei, the Taizu led an army against Hada.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the ninth month, a dingwei day, the Taizu led his army against Hada.

sentences.zh: 貝勒舒爾哈齊請爲前鋒，薄孟格布祿所居城。

translations.literal: Beile Šurhaci asked to be vanguard and approached Menggebulu's city.
translations.idiomatic: Beile Šurhaci asked to lead the vanguard and pressed close to Menggebulu's city.

sentences.zh: 兵出，舒爾哈齊使告太祖曰：「彼城兵出矣！」

translations.literal: When troops came out, Šurhaci sent to tell the Taizu: "The enemy city has sent out troops!"
translations.idiomatic: When troops came out, Šurhaci sent word to the Taizu, "The enemy city has sent out troops!"

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「豈爲此城無兵而來耶？」

translations.literal: The Taizu said: "Did I come because this city has no troops?"
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu said, "Did I come because this city had no troops?"

sentences.zh: 躬督兵進。

translations.literal: He personally supervised the advance of troops.
translations.idiomatic: He personally led the advance.

sentences.zh: 舒爾哈齊兵塞道，太祖軍循城行，城上發矢多傷者，遂攻城，癸丑，克之。

translations.literal: Šurhaci's troops blocked the road; the Taizu's army went along the city walls; many were wounded by arrows from the walls; they then besieged the city; on guichou it was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Šurhaci's troops blocked the road; the Taizu's army marched along the walls, and many were wounded by arrows from above; they then besieged the city and took it on a guichou day.

sentences.zh: 揚古利生得孟格布祿，太祖命勿殺，召入謁，賜以所御貂帽、豹裘，置帳中。

translations.literal: Yangguli captured Menggebulu alive; the Taizu ordered him not killed, summoned him to audience, bestowed his own sable cap and leopard fur, and placed him in the tent.
translations.idiomatic: Yangguli took Menggebulu alive; the Taizu ordered him spared, summoned him to audience, gave him his own sable cap and leopard fur, and kept him in his tent.

sentences.zh: 既，孟格布祿與噶蓋謀爲亂，事洩，乃殺之。

translations.literal: Later Menggebulu plotted rebellion with Gagai; the matter leaked out and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Menggebulu plotted rebellion with Gagai; when the plot was exposed he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 二十九年春正月，太祖以女妻孟格布祿子吳爾古代，明使來讓，太祖遣吳爾古代還所部。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the twenty-ninth year, the Taizu gave a daughter in marriage to Menggebulu's son Wu'ergudai; the Ming sent to reprove; the Taizu sent Wu'ergudai back to his tribe.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring of the twenty-ninth year the Taizu gave a daughter in marriage to Menggebulu's son Wu'ergudai; when the Ming protested, he sent Wu'ergudai back to his tribe.

sentences.zh: 納林布祿歸所掠敕六十道，請於明，補雙貢如故事。

translations.literal: Nalinbulu returned sixty plundered patents and requested the Ming restore double tribute as of old.
translations.idiomatic: Nalinbulu returned sixty plundered patents and asked the Ming to restore the double tribute of former times.

sentences.zh: 已而，納林布祿復糾蒙古掠哈達。

translations.literal: Later Nalinbulu again joined Mongols in raiding Hada.
translations.idiomatic: Later Nalinbulu again joined the Mongols in raiding Hada.

sentences.zh: 哈達饑，乞糴於明，明不與，至鬻妻子、奴僕以食。

translations.literal: Hada was starving and begged grain from the Ming; the Ming did not give it; they even sold wives, children, and slaves for food.
translations.idiomatic: Hada starved and begged grain from the Ming, who refused; people even sold wives, children, and slaves for food.

sentences.zh: 太祖周恤之，遂以吳爾古代歸。

translations.literal: The Taizu succored them and returned Wu'ergudai.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu gave them relief and sent Wu'ergudai back.

sentences.zh: 哈達亡。

translations.literal: Hada perished.
translations.idiomatic: Hada was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 楊吉砮，葉赫部長，孝慈高皇后父也。

translations.literal: Yangginu was Yehhe chieftain and father of the Empress Xiaoci Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Yangginu was chief of Yehhe and father of the Empress Xiaoci Gao.

sentences.zh: 其先出自蒙古，姓土默特氏，滅納喇部據其地，遂以地爲姓；

translations.literal: His ancestors came from Mongolia, surname Tümed; they destroyed the Nara tribe and occupied their lands, taking the land as surname;
translations.idiomatic: His line came from Mongolia, of the Tümed clan; they destroyed the Nara tribe, seized its lands, and took the place as their surname;

sentences.zh: 後遷葉赫河岸，因號葉赫。

translations.literal: later they moved to the banks of the Yehhe River and so were called Yehhe.
translations.idiomatic: later they moved to the Yehhe River and took the name Yehhe.

sentences.zh: 其貢於明，取道鎭北關，地近北，故明謂之北關。

translations.literal: In paying tribute to the Ming they took the Zhenbei Pass route; the lands lay toward the north, so the Ming called them the Northern Pass faction.
translations.idiomatic: They paid tribute to the Ming through Zhenbei Pass; because their lands lay far to the north, the Ming called them the Northern Pass branch.

sentences.zh: 始祖星根達爾漢生席爾克明噶圖，席爾克明噶圖生齊爾噶尼。

translations.literal: The founding ancestor Xinggendaerhan begat Xierkeminggatu; Xierkeminggatu begat Qiergani.
translations.idiomatic: The founder Xinggendaerhan was followed by Xierkeminggatu and then Qiergani.

sentences.zh: 正德初，齊爾噶尼數盜邊，斬開原市。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhengde reign, Qiergani repeatedly raided the border and markets at Kaiyuan were suspended.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Zhengde era Qiergani raided the frontier repeatedly, and trade at Kaiyuan was cut off.

sentences.zh: 八年，其子褚孔格糾他酋加哈復爲亂，旋就撫，授達喜木魯都督僉事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, his son Zhukongge joined other chiefs including Jiaha in rebellion again; he soon submitted and was appointed Daximulu Vice Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year his son Zhukongge joined other chiefs such as Jiaha in another revolt; he soon submitted and was made Daximulu Vice Military Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 褚孔格阻兵數反覆，爲哈達部長旺濟外蘭所殺，明賜敕書及所屬諸寨，皆爲所奪。

translations.literal: Zhukongge repeatedly took up arms and turned back and forth; he was killed by the Hada chieftain Wangji Wailan; the Ming-bestowed patents and all his stockaded villages were seized.
translations.idiomatic: Zhukongge repeatedly rebelled and submitted; the Hada chief Wangji Wailan killed him and seized the Ming patents and all his stockaded villages.

sentences.zh: 褚孔格子太杵。

translations.literal: Zhukongge had a son Taichu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhukongge had a son named Taichu.

sentences.zh: 太杵子二：長，清佳砮；

translations.literal: Taichu had two sons: the eldest, Qingjianu;
translations.idiomatic: Taichu had two sons: the elder Qingjianu;

sentences.zh: 次即楊吉砮。

translations.literal: the second was Yangginu.
translations.idiomatic: the younger was Yangginu.

sentences.zh: 能撫諸部，依險築二城，相距可數里，清佳砮居西城，楊吉砮居東城，皆稱貝勒。

translations.literal: They were able to pacify the tribes, built two cities on defensible ground a few li apart; Qingjianu dwelled in the western city, Yangginu in the eastern city; both styled themselves beile.
translations.idiomatic: They pacified the tribes and built two fortified cities a few li apart; Qingjianu held the western city and Yangginu the eastern, and both styled themselves beile.

sentences.zh: 明人以譯音，謂之「二奴」。

translations.literal: The Ming, by transliteration, called them the "Two Slaves."
translations.idiomatic: The Ming, by transliteration, called them the "Two Slaves."

sentences.zh: 是時哈達萬汗方強，楊吉砮弟兄事萬謹，萬納其女弟溫姐，藉勢寖驕，數糾建州王杲侵明邊。

translations.literal: At this time Khan Wan of Hada was strong; the brothers Yangginu served Wan scrupulously; Wan took Qingjianu's younger sister Wenjie; relying on his power they grew arrogant and repeatedly incited Jianzhou's Wang Gao to raid the Ming border.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Khan Wan of Hada was at his height; the brothers served him faithfully; Wan took Wenjie, Qingjianu's younger sister, in marriage, and emboldened by his power they grew arrogant and repeatedly incited Wang Gao of Jianzhou to raid the Ming frontier.

sentences.zh: 明討王杲，而清佳砮，楊吉砮不與，蓋萬實庇之，既又以女妻楊吉砮。

translations.literal: When the Ming punished Wang Gao, Qingjianu and Yangginu did not join, for Wan in fact sheltered them; he also gave a daughter in marriage to Yangginu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ming moved against Wang Gao, Qingjianu and Yangginu did not take part, for Wan sheltered them and had also given Yangginu a daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 然楊吉砮兄弟日夜思復先世褚孔格之仇，怨萬。

translations.literal: Yet the brothers Yangginu day and night thought to avenge their ancestor Zhukongge and resented Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the brothers brooded day and night on avenging their forebear Zhukongge and bore Wan a grudge.

sentences.zh: 會萬老，勢衰，楊吉砮復婚於哈屯恍惚太，以隙復故地季勒諸寨。

translations.literal: When Wan grew old and his power waned, Yangginu again married into the Haton Huanghu Tai clan and on the opportunity recovered the old stockades of Jile and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Wan aged and weakened, Yangginu married again into the Haton Huanghu Tai clan and seized the chance to recover the old stockades of Jile and the rest.

sentences.zh: 萬子扈爾干所屬白虎赤等先後叛歸楊吉砮，楊吉砮勢日盛，萬遂以憂憤死。

translations.literal: Baihuchi and others under Wan's son Huergan successively defected to Yangginu; Yangginu's power grew daily, and Wan died of grief and rage.
translations.idiomatic: Baihuchi and others under Wan's son Huergan defected to Yangginu one after another; Yangginu's power swelled, and Wan died of grief and rage.

sentences.zh: 死而諸子內爭，其庶孽康古魯亡抵清佳砮，清佳砮妻以女，益間萬子孫使自相圖。

translations.literal: After his death his sons contended within; his bastard son Kanguru fled to Qingjianu, who gave him a daughter in marriage, further setting Wan's descendants against one another.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his sons fought among themselves; his bastard Kanguru fled to Qingjianu, who gave him a daughter in marriage and further set Wan's descendants at one another's throats.

sentences.zh: 既而太祖兵起，嘗如葉赫，楊吉砮顧知爲非常人，謂太祖曰：「我有幼女，俟其長，當使事君。」

translations.literal: Later when the Taizu raised his army, he once went to Yehhe; Yangginu perceived he was no ordinary man and said to the Taizu: "I have a young daughter; when she grows up I shall have her serve you."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Taizu raised his army, he visited Yehhe; Yangginu saw that he was no ordinary man and said, "I have a young daughter; when she is grown I shall give her to you."

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「君欲結姻盟，盍以年已長者妻我？」

translations.literal: The Taizu said: "If you wish to form a marriage alliance, why not give me your elder daughter?"
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu said, "If you wish an alliance by marriage, why not give me your elder daughter?"

sentences.zh: 楊吉砮對曰：「我雖有長女，恐未爲嘉偶。

translations.literal: Yangginu replied: "Although I have an elder daughter, I fear she would not be a worthy match.
translations.idiomatic: Yangginu replied, "I do have an elder daughter, but I fear she would not be a worthy match.

sentences.zh: 幼女端重，始足爲君配耳。」

translations.literal: My young daughter is dignified and would alone suffice as your consort."
translations.idiomatic: My younger daughter is dignified; only she is fit to be your consort."

sentences.zh: ​​太祖遂納聘焉。

translations.literal: The Taizu then accepted betrothal gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu then accepted the betrothal.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十一年，楊吉砮弟兄率白虎赤，益以煖兔、恍惚太所部萬騎，襲敗孟格布祿，斬三百​​級，掠甲胄一百五十；

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Wanli, the brothers Yangginu led Baihuchi, with ten thousand horsemen of Nuantu and Huanghu Tai added, raided and defeated Menggebulu, beheading three hundred heads and seizing one hundred fifty suits of armor;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Wanli the brothers Yangginu led Baihuchi and ten thousand horsemen under Nuantu and Huanghu Tai against Menggebulu, defeated him, took three hundred heads, and seized one hundred fifty suits of armor;

sentences.zh: 益借猛骨太、那木塞兵，焚躪孟格布祿所部室廬、田稼殆盡。

translations.literal: they further borrowed troops of Menggutai and Namusai, burning and trampling Menggebulu's dwellings and crops nearly to destruction.
translations.idiomatic: they borrowed troops from Menggutai and Namusai as well and burned and trampled Menggebulu's dwellings and crops almost to nothing.

sentences.zh: 明分巡副使任天祚使齎布帛及鐵釜，犒楊吉砮兄弟，諭罷兵。

translations.literal: The Ming circuit patrol vice commissioner Ren Tianzuo sent cloth, silks, and iron cauldrons to reward the brothers Yangginu and instruct them to cease fighting.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming patrol vice commissioner Ren Tianzuo sent cloth, silks, and iron cauldrons to reward the brothers and ordered them to stop fighting.

sentences.zh: 楊吉砮兄弟言：「必得敕書盡轄孟格布祿等然後已。」

translations.literal: The brothers Yangginu said: "We must have patents putting Menggebulu and others wholly under our authority before we stop."
translations.idiomatic: The brothers said, "We will not stop until we have patents placing Menggebulu and the rest wholly under our authority."

sentences.zh: 既，復焚孟格布祿及其仲兄所分莊各十，岱善莊一，脅所屬百餘人去。

translations.literal: Afterward they again burned ten estates each of Menggebulu and his second brother's allotment and one of Daishan's, and coerced more than a hundred followers to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward they burned ten estates each belonging to Menggebulu and his second brother and one of Daishan's, and forced more than a hundred of their followers to defect.

sentences.zh: 既，又以恍惚太二千騎馳廣順關，攻下沙大亮寨，俘三百人，挾兵邀貢敕。

translations.literal: Again with two thousand horsemen of Huanghu Tai they galloped to Guangshun Pass, took Shadaliang stockade, captured three hundred people, and with armed force demanded tribute patents.
translations.idiomatic: Again they galloped to Guangshun Pass with two thousand horsemen of Huanghu Tai, took Shadaliang stockade, captured three hundred people, and demanded tribute patents at sword point.

sentences.zh: 十二年，巡撫李松與總兵李成梁謀誅楊吉砮兄弟，哈達亦以請。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Censor Li Song and Commander Li Chenglang plotted to kill the brothers Yangginu; Hada also requested this.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Censor Li Song and Commander Li Chenglang plotted to kill the brothers Yangginu, and Hada asked for the same.

sentences.zh: 明制，凡諸部​​互市，築牆規市場，謂之「市圈」。

translations.literal: By Ming regulation, when tribes traded with one another they built walls to define the market ground, called a "market pen."
translations.idiomatic: Under Ming practice, when tribes came to trade, a walled market ground was built, called a "market pen."

sentences.zh: 成梁使召楊吉砮弟兄，當賜敕賞賚，乃伏兵中固城，距開原可四十里，待其至。

translations.literal: Chenglang sent to summon the brothers Yangginu, saying patents and rewards would be bestowed; he hid troops at Zhonggu City, about forty li from Kaiyuan, and waited for their arrival.
translations.idiomatic: Chenglang summoned the brothers, saying patents and rewards awaited them, and hid troops at Zhonggu City, about forty li from Kaiyuan, to wait for them.

sentences.zh: 已而楊吉砮弟兄挾恍惚太二千騎擐甲叩鎭北關，守備霍九皋遣使讓之曰：「若來就撫，甲騎數千何爲者？」

translations.literal: Soon the brothers Yangginu came with two thousand armored horsemen of Huanghu Tai to knock at Zhenbei Pass; the garrison commander Huo Jiugao sent to reprove them: "If you come to submit, what need of several thousand armored horsemen?"
translations.idiomatic: Soon the brothers came to Zhenbei Pass with two thousand armored horsemen of Huanghu Tai; the garrison commander Huo Jiugao sent to reprove them, "If you come to submit, why bring several thousand armored horsemen?"

sentences.zh: 楊吉砮兄弟乃請以三百騎入圈。

translations.literal: The brothers Yangginu then asked to enter the pen with three hundred horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers then asked to enter the pen with three hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 李松令參將宿振武、李寧等夾城四隅爲伏，戒軍中曰：「虜入圈，聽撫則張幟，按甲毋動；

translations.literal: Li Song ordered Brigade Generals Su Zhenwu, Li Ning, and others to set ambushes at the four corners of the walled compound, instructing the army: "When the barbarians enter the pen, if they submit, raise banners and hold your armor still;
translations.idiomatic: Li Song ordered Brigade Generals Su Zhenwu, Li Ning, and others to set ambushes at the four corners and told the army, "When the barbarians enter the pen, if they submit, raise the banners and hold still;

sentences.zh: 不則鳴礮，皆鼓行而前，急擊之勿失。」

translations.literal: otherwise fire the cannon, all advance beating drums, and strike them swiftly without fail."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise fire the cannon, advance with drums, and strike them swiftly without fail."

sentences.zh: 松與任天祚坐南樓，使九皋諭楊吉砮兄弟。

translations.literal: Li Song and Ren Tianzuo sat in the south tower and had Jiugao instruct the brothers Yangginu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Song and Ren Tianzuo sat in the south tower and had Jiugao address the brothers.

sentences.zh: 楊吉砮兄弟則益兵，以精騎三千屯鎭北關，而以三百騎入圈。

translations.literal: The brothers Yangginu meanwhile increased their forces, stationing three thousand elite horsemen at Zhenbei Pass while three hundred entered the pen.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers meanwhile reinforced their force, leaving three thousand elite horsemen at Zhenbei Pass while three hundred entered the pen.

sentences.zh: 楊吉砮兄弟請敕書部勒孟格布祿等，九皋譙讓之，漸急，楊吉砮兄弟瞋目，語不馴，李松奮髯抵几叱之。

translations.literal: The brothers demanded patents to control Menggebulu and others; Jiugao rebuked them increasingly sharply; the brothers glared, their words insubordinate; Li Song bristled and struck the table shouting at them.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers demanded patents to control Menggebulu and the rest; Jiugao rebuked them ever more sharply; they glared and answered insolently; Li Song struck the table and shouted them down.

sentences.zh: 九皋麾楊吉砮等下馬，楊吉砮目從者白虎赤，白虎赤拔刀擊九皋，微中右臂。

translations.literal: Jiugao ordered Yangginu and the others to dismount; Yangginu signaled his follower Baihuchi, who drew his blade and struck Jiugao, slightly wounding his right arm.
translations.idiomatic: Jiugao ordered them to dismount; Yangginu signaled Baihuchi, who drew his blade and struck Jiugao, slightly wounding his right arm.

sentences.zh: 九皋還擊楊吉砮從者一騎踣，餘騎羣噪擊明兵。

translations.literal: Jiugao struck back and felled one of Yangginu's horsemen; the rest clamored and attacked the Ming troops.
translations.idiomatic: Jiugao struck back and cut down one horseman; the rest raised a clamor and attacked the Ming troops.

sentences.zh: 軍中礮如雷，伏盡起，遂殺清佳砮、楊吉砮、白虎赤、清佳砮子兀孫孛羅、楊吉砮子哈兒哈麻，及諸從者，斬三百十有一級。

translations.literal: Cannons thundered in the army and all ambushes rose; they killed Qingjianu, Yangginu, Baihuchi, Qingjianu's son Wusun Boluo, Yangginu's son Ha'erhama, and all followers, beheading three hundred eleven heads.
translations.idiomatic: Cannons thundered, the ambushes sprang up, and they killed Qingjianu, Yangginu, Baihuchi, Qingjianu's son Wusun Boluo, Yangginu's son Ha'erhama, and their followers, taking three hundred eleven heads.

sentences.zh: 勒兵馳出關，成梁先自中固城至，圍擊葉赫軍，斬千五百二十一級，奪馬千七百有三，遂深入楊吉砮弟兄所居寨。

translations.literal: Troops galloped out of the pass; Chenglang had already come from Zhonggu City and surrounded the Yehhe army, beheading one thousand five hundred twenty-one heads and seizing one thousand seven hundred three horses; they then penetrated deep into the brothers Yangginu's stockaded residence.
translations.idiomatic: Troops galloped out of the pass; Chenglang had already come from Zhonggu City, surrounded the Yehhe army, took one thousand five hundred twenty-one heads and one thousand seven hundred three horses, and pressed deep into the brothers' stockaded residence.

sentences.zh: 師合圍，旦日，諸酋出寨門蒲伏，請受孟格布祿約束，刑白馬攢刀爲誓，成梁引師還。

translations.literal: The army closed the encirclement; at dawn the chiefs came prostrate from the stockade gate, asking to accept Menggebulu's authority; they slew a white horse and piled knives in oath; Chenglang withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: The army closed the ring; at dawn the chiefs came prostrate from the gate, asking to submit to Menggebulu; they sacrificed a white horse and piled knives in oath; Chenglang withdrew.

sentences.zh: 自是葉赫不敢出兵窺塞擾哈達爲亂。

translations.literal: From then on Yehhe did not dare send troops to spy on the border and disturb Hada into rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Yehhe did not dare raid the frontier or stir trouble against Hada.

sentences.zh: 明總督張佳胤等以陣斬「二奴」聞，成梁、松、天祚、九皋、振武、寧予廕進秩有差。

translations.literal: The Ming grand coordinator Zhang Jiayin and others reported the killing of the "Two Slaves" in battle; Chenglang, Song, Tianzuo, Jiugao, Zhenwu, and Ning received differing promotions of rank and hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Zhang Jiayin reported the killing of the "Two Slaves" in battle; Chenglang, Song, Tianzuo, Jiugao, Zhenwu, and Ning received differing promotions and hereditary privileges.

sentences.zh: 居數年，清佳砮子布寨、楊吉砮子納林布祿繼爲貝勒，收餘燼，謀傾哈達報世讎，挾以兒鄧數侵掠，闌入威遠堡。

translations.literal: After several years, Qingjianu's son Buzhai and Yangginu's son Nalinbulu succeeded as beile, gathered the embers, plotted to overthrow Hada and avenge the feud of generations, and with Erdeng repeatedly raided, breaking into Weiyuan Fort.
translations.idiomatic: After several years Qingjianu's son Buzhai and Yangginu's son Nalinbulu became beile, gathered what remained, plotted to destroy Hada and avenge an old feud, and with Erdeng raided repeatedly, breaking into Weiyuan Fort.

sentences.zh: 納林布祿尤狂悖，要貢敕如其諸父，頻歲糾恍惚太攻岱善不已；

translations.literal: Nalinbulu was especially arrogant and defiant, demanding tribute patents like his uncles, year after year joining Huanghu Tai in attacking Daishan without cease;
translations.idiomatic: Nalinbulu was especially arrogant, demanding tribute patents like his uncles and year after year joining Huanghu Tai in unceasing attacks on Daishan;

sentences.zh: 且因其姑溫姐煽孟格布祿、康古魯圖岱善，俾哈達內訌。

translations.literal: and through his aunt Wenjie incited Menggebulu and Kanguru to plot against Daishan, causing internal strife in Hada.
translations.idiomatic: and through his aunt Wenjie incited Menggebulu and Kanguru to plot against Daishan, sowing civil strife in Hada.

sentences.zh: 會明助岱善，襲執康古魯。

translations.literal: When the Ming aided Daishan, they raided and captured Kanguru.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ming aided Daishan, they raided and captured Kanguru.

sentences.zh: 十六年二月，巡撫顧養謙決策討布寨、納林布祿。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixteenth year, Censor Gu Yangqian decided on a campaign against Buzhai and Nalinbulu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixteenth year Censor Gu Yangqian decided to campaign against Buzhai and Nalinbulu.

sentences.zh: 成梁帥師至海州，雪初消，人馬行淖中，馬足膠不可拔。

translations.literal: Chenglang led his army to Haizhou; the snow had just melted and men and horses marched through mire; horses' hooves stuck in the mud and could not be pulled free.
translations.idiomatic: Chenglang led his army to Haizhou; the snow had just melted, and men and horses sank in the mud until their hooves stuck fast.

sentences.zh: 成梁計擊虜利月明，軍抵開原已下弦，不如三月往，遂壁海州，養謙壁遼陽。

translations.literal: Chenglang calculated that striking the enemy favored bright moonlight; the army reached Kaiyuan after the last quarter; it were better to go in the third month; he therefore encamped at Haizhou and Yangqian encamped at Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chenglang reckoned that raiding the enemy favored a bright moon; the army reached Kaiyuan after the last quarter of the moon, so it were better to wait until the third month; he encamped at Haizhou and Yangqian at Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 是歲，河西大饑，斗米錢三千，菽二千，發海州、遼陽穀贍軍。

translations.literal: That year a great famine struck west of the river; a dou of millet cost three thousand cash and beans two thousand; grain from Haizhou and Liaoyang was issued to provision the army.
translations.idiomatic: That year a great famine struck west of the river; a dou of millet cost three thousand cash and beans two thousand; grain from Haizhou and Liaoyang was issued to feed the army.

sentences.zh: 月將晦，成樑自海州乘傳出，三月十有三日，至開原。

translations.literal: As the month neared its end, Chenglang left Haizhou by relay post; on the thirteenth day of the third month he reached Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Near month's end Chenglang left Haizhou by relay post and reached Kaiyuan on the thirteenth day of the third month.

sentences.zh: 令岱善軍以白布綴肩際爲幟，雞鳴，發威遠堡，行三十里，至葉赫屬酋落羅寨。

translations.literal: He ordered Daishan's army to mark their shoulders with white cloth as banners; at cockcrow they set out from Weiyuan Fort, marched thirty li, and reached the stockade of Luoluo, a Yehhe subordinate chief.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Daishan's army to fix white cloth on their shoulders as banners; at cockcrow they left Weiyuan Fort, marched thirty li, and reached the stockade of Luoluo, a Yehhe subordinate chief.

sentences.zh: 成梁使召落羅，落羅駭兵至，迎謁，命以一幟樹寨門，材官十人守之，戒諸軍毋犯；

translations.literal: Chenglang sent to summon Luoluo; Luoluo, alarmed that troops had come, came out to meet him; Chenglang ordered one banner planted at the stockade gate and ten engineering officers to guard it, forbidding the army to violate it;
translations.idiomatic: Chenglang summoned Luoluo; alarmed by the army's arrival, Luoluo came out to meet him; Chenglang planted a banner at the stockade gate, left ten engineering officers to guard it, and forbade the army to harm it;

sentences.zh: 挾落羅及其從者三騎俱，又行三十里，至葉赫城下。

translations.literal: He took Luoluo and his three horsemen followers along, marched another thirty li, and reached below Yehhe city.
translations.idiomatic: He took Luoluo and his three followers along, marched another thirty li, and came beneath Yehhe city.

sentences.zh: 布塞棄西城，奔納林布祿，併兵以拒，其眾與明軍夾道馳，明軍不敢先發。

translations.literal: Buzhai abandoned the western city and fled to Nalinbulu; they combined forces to resist; their troops and the Ming army galloped along the road on either side; the Ming army did not dare strike first.
translations.idiomatic: Buzhai abandoned the western city and fled to Nalinbulu; they combined forces to resist; their horsemen and the Ming army galloped along the road on either side, and the Ming did not dare strike first.

sentences.zh: 二酋麾其騎突明軍，殺三人，成梁乃縱兵擊之。

translations.literal: The two chiefs directed their horsemen to charge the Ming army, killing three men; Chenglang then unleashed his troops to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: The two chiefs sent their horsemen charging into the Ming line, killing three men; Chenglang then unleashed his troops.

sentences.zh: 游擊將軍吳希漢先驅，流矢集於面，創甚，弟希周奮起，斬虜騎射希漢者，亦被創。

translations.literal: Patrol General Wu Xihan led the van; flying arrows clustered on his face and he was badly wounded; his younger brother Xizhou sprang up and cut down the barbarian horseman who had shot Xihan, and was also wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Patrol General Wu Xihan led the van; arrows clustered on his face and he was badly wounded; his brother Xizhou sprang up and cut down the horseman who had shot him, and was wounded as well.

sentences.zh: 明軍如牆進，葉赫兵退入城守。

translations.literal: The Ming army advanced like a wall; the Yehhe troops withdrew into the city to defend.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming army advanced like a wall; the Yehhe troops fell back into the city to defend it.

sentences.zh: 城以石爲郭，郭內外重疊障，以巨桁爲栅。

translations.literal: The city used stone for its outer wall; inside and outside the wall overlapping barriers were built with huge beams as palisades.
translations.idiomatic: The city had a stone outer wall; inside and out were layered barriers and palisades of huge beams.

sentences.zh: 城中有山，鑿山周遭爲坂，絕峻，爲羅城其上，外以石，內以木，又二重，中構八角樓，置妻孥、財貨。

translations.literal: Within the city was a hill; the hill was cut around into a slope, exceedingly steep, and a secondary wall was built upon it; stone without, wood within, in two layers; an octagonal tower was built in the center, storing wives, children, and wealth.
translations.idiomatic: A hill rose within the city; its sides were cut into a steep slope, and a secondary wall was built on top, stone without and wood within in two layers; at the center stood an octagonal tower holding wives, children, and treasure.

sentences.zh: 明師攻二日，破郭外栅二重。

translations.literal: The Ming army attacked for two days and broke two layers of palisades outside the wall.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming army attacked for two days and broke two layers of palisades outside the wall.

sentences.zh: 城上木石雜下，先登者輒死，城堅不可拔。

translations.literal: Timber and stones rained mixed from the walls; those who climbed first died at once; the city was strong and could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Timber and stones rained from the walls; the first to climb died at once; the city was too strong to storm.

sentences.zh: 成梁乃斂兵，發巨礮擊城，城壞，穿樓斷桁，葉赫兵死者無算，殲其酋把當亥，斬級五百五十四，城中皆號泣。

translations.literal: Chenglang then drew in his troops and fired great cannon at the city; the city was broken, the tower pierced and beams snapped; Yehhe soldiers died beyond counting; their chief Badangai was destroyed; five hundred fifty-four heads were taken; all within the city wailed.
translations.idiomatic: Chenglang then drew back his troops and bombarded the city with great cannon; the walls broke, the tower was pierced and beams shattered; Yehhe soldiers died beyond counting; their chief Badangai was killed; five hundred fifty-four heads were taken; the whole city wailed.

sentences.zh: 明軍車載雲梯至，直立，齊其內城，將置巨礮其上。

translations.literal: The Ming army carted cloud ladders to the spot, set them upright, and aligned them with the inner wall, intending to mount great cannon upon them.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming army brought up siege ladders by cart, raised them upright against the inner wall, and prepared to place heavy cannon on top.

sentences.zh: 二酋始大懼，出城乞降，請與南關分敕入貢。

translations.literal: The two chiefs then were greatly afraid; they came out of the city to beg surrender and asked to divide the patents for tribute with the South Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The two chiefs were seized with fear. They came out to surrender and asked that patents for tribute be shared with the South Gate.

sentences.zh: 成梁令​​毋攻，燔雲梯，戒諸軍毋發其窖粟，遂引師還。

translations.literal: Chenglang ordered that there be no attack, burned the cloud ladders, warned the troops not to open their cellar grain, and then withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: Chenglang forbade an assault, burned the ladders, ordered his men not to touch the grain in the cellars, and marched away.

sentences.zh: 四月朔，釋康古魯遣還，因進葉赫使者諭曰：「往若效順，朝廷賞不薄。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fourth month he released Kang Guru and sent him back, then advanced Yehhe envoys and instructed them, saying: "If you had submitted in the past, the court's rewards would not have been slight.
translations.idiomatic: On the first of the fourth month he released Kang Guru and sent him home, then received Yehhe envoys and told them: "Had you submitted before, the court would have rewarded you generously.

sentences.zh: 江上遠夷以貂皮、人參至，必藉若以通。

translations.literal: Distant tribes along the river bring sable pelts and ginseng; they must rely on you to pass through.
translations.idiomatic: River tribes far upstream bring sable and ginseng; they must pass through your lands to trade.

sentences.zh: 若布帛、米鹽、農器仰給於我，耕稼圍獵，坐收木枲、松實、山澤之利，爲惠大矣。

translations.literal: If cloth, rice, salt, and farm tools all depend on us, you may farm, hunt, and sit collecting hemp, pine nuts, and the profits of mountains and marshes—a great boon.
translations.idiomatic: You depend on us for cloth, grain, salt, and tools; you farm and hunt while reaping hemp, pine nuts, and mountain wealth—a great benefit.

sentences.zh: 今貢事絕，江上夷道梗，皆怨若。

translations.literal: Now tribute has ceased and the river tribes' road is blocked; all resent you.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute has stopped and the river trade is choked off; everyone blames you.

sentences.zh: 我第傳檄諸部，斬二酋頭來，俾爲長，可無煩兵誅也。

translations.literal: I need only send orders to the tribes: bring the two chiefs' heads and I will make you chief—no need to trouble the army with punishment.
translations.idiomatic: I need only proclaim to the tribes: send the two chiefs' heads and I will set you up as leader—then no army need be sent against you.

sentences.zh: 今貸若，若何以報？」

translations.literal: Now I spare you—how will you repay me?"
translations.idiomatic: I spare you today—what will you give in return?"

sentences.zh: 遂與哈達均敕。

translations.literal: He then divided the patents evenly with Hada.
translations.idiomatic: He then shared the patents equally with Hada.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，賜海西諸部敕，自都督至百戶，凡九百九十九道。

translations.literal: In early Yongle the Haixi tribes were granted patents from Commander down to Centurion—nine hundred ninety-nine in all.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongle reign the Haixi tribes received patents from commander to centurion—nine hundred ninety-nine in all.

sentences.zh: 至是，畀哈達、葉赫分領之，以哈達效順，使贏其一。

translations.literal: At this time these were given to Hada and Yehhe to divide and administer; because Hada had submitted, it was made to win one share more.
translations.idiomatic: Now they were divided between Hada and Yehhe; because Hada had submitted, it was given the larger share.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，納林布祿送其女弟歸太祖，太祖率諸貝勒迎之，大宴成禮，是爲孝慈高皇后。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn Nalinbulu sent his younger sister to the Taizu; the Taizu led all the beiles to welcome her, held a great feast to complete the rites—this was Empress Xiaoci Gao.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the ninth month, Nalinbulu sent his younger sister to the Taizu. The Taizu and his beiles went out to welcome her, feasted, and completed the marriage—she became Empress Xiaoci Gao.

sentences.zh: 十九年，納林布祿令宜爾當阿、擺斯漢<ref>“宜爾當阿、擺斯漢”，原典作“宜爾當、阿擺斯漢”，誤。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Nalinbulu ordered Yierdang'a and Baisihan [the original text wrongly reads "Yierdang, Abaisihan"].
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Nalinbulu dispatched Yierdang'a and Baisihan as envoys [the received text misdivides their names as "Yierdang" and "Abaisihan"].

sentences.zh: </ref>使於太祖，且曰：「扈倫諸部與滿洲語言相通，宜合五爲一。

translations.literal: to go to the Taizu, saying: "The Hulun tribes and the Manchu share a language; the five should be united as one.
translations.idiomatic: to the Taizu with this message: "The Hulun tribes speak the same tongue as the Manchu; the five ought to become one.

sentences.zh: 今屬地爾多我寡，額爾敏、扎庫木二地，盍以一與我！」

translations.literal: Now in territory you are many and I few—the two places Ermin and Zhakumu: why not give me one!"
translations.idiomatic: Your lands are vast and mine are small—of Ermin and Zhakumu, give me one!"

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「我爲滿洲，爾爲扈倫，各有分地。

translations.literal: The Taizu said: "I am Manchu and you are Hulun; each has his allotted lands.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu replied: "I am Manchu and you are Hulun; each keeps his own domain.

sentences.zh: 我毋爾取，爾毋我爭。

translations.literal: I will not take from you; you will not contend with me.
translations.idiomatic: I will not seize yours; you must not seize mine.

sentences.zh: 地非牛馬比，豈可分遺？

translations.literal: Land is not like cattle and horses—how can it be carved up and given away?
translations.idiomatic: Land is not cattle to be parceled out—how can it be divided and handed over?

sentences.zh: 爾等皆知政，不能諫爾主，奈何强顏來相瀆耶！」

translations.literal: You all understand governance yet cannot remonstrate with your lord—how dare you come shamelessly to insult me!"
translations.idiomatic: You know better yet will not counsel your master—how dare you come here to insult me!"

sentences.zh: 遣其使還。

translations.literal: He sent their envoys back.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the envoys away.

sentences.zh: 既而納林布祿又令尼喀里、圖爾德偕哈達、輝發二部使​​者復至，太祖與之宴。

translations.literal: Before long Nalinbulu again sent Nikali and Tuerde together with envoys from the Hada and Huifa departments; the Taizu feasted with them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Nalinbulu sent Nikali and Tuerde with envoys from Hada and Huifa; the Taizu entertained them.

sentences.zh: 圖爾德起而請曰：「我主有傳語，恐爲貝勒怒。」

translations.literal: Tuerde rose and said: "My lord has a message he fears will anger the beile."
translations.idiomatic: Tuerde rose and said: "My lord has words to relay, but fears they will anger you."

sentences.zh: 太祖問：「爾主何語？

translations.literal: The Taizu asked: "What words from your lord?
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu asked: "What does your lord say?

sentences.zh: 我不爾責。」

translations.literal: I will not blame you."
translations.idiomatic: Speak freely—I will not hold it against you."

sentences.zh: 圖爾德曰：「我主言曩欲分爾地，爾靳不與。

translations.literal: Tuerde said: "My lord says that when he wished to divide your land, you were stingy and would not give.
translations.idiomatic: Tuerde said: "My lord says you refused when he asked to share your territory.

sentences.zh: 儻兩國舉兵相攻，我能入爾境，爾安能蹈我地乎？」

translations.literal: If the two states raise armies and attack each other, I can enter your borders—how can you tread my land?"
translations.idiomatic: If we go to war, I can march into your country—can you set foot in mine?"

sentences.zh: 太祖大怒，引佩刀斷案曰：「爾葉赫諸舅，盍嘗躬在行間，馬首相交，裂甲毀冑，堪一劇戰耶？

translations.literal: The Taizu was furious; he drew his sword and split the table, saying: "You Yehhe uncles—have you ever stood in the ranks yourselves, horses' heads meeting, armor torn and helmets shattered, worth one fierce battle?
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu flew into a rage, drew his blade, and smashed the table. "You Yehhe kinsmen—have you ever fought hand to hand, horses crashing together, mail ripped and helms broken—ever fought a real battle?

sentences.zh: 哈達惟內訌，故爾等得乘隙掩襲，何視我若彼易與也！

translations.literal: Hada had only internal strife, so you could seize the gap and raid—why do you treat me as easy prey!
translations.idiomatic: You only beat Hada because it was torn by civil war—why think me as weak as they were!

sentences.zh: 吾視蹈爾地，如入無人境，晝即不來，夜亦可往，爾其若我何！」

translations.literal: I regard treading your land as entering an empty country—if not by day, then by night I can go; what can you do to me!"
translations.idiomatic: Crossing your land is like walking through an empty land—come day or night whenever I please; what can you do?"

sentences.zh: 因詆布寨、納林布祿父見殺於明，至不得收其骨，奈何出大言，以其語爲書，遣巴克什阿林察報之。

translations.literal: He then reviled Buzhai and Nalinbulu because their fathers had been killed by the Ming and their bones could not even be recovered—yet they dared such grand talk; he set the words down in a letter and sent the clerk Alincha to deliver it.
translations.idiomatic: He mocked Buzhai and Nalinbulu: their fathers were killed by the Ming and their bones never recovered—yet they boasted so. He wrote the reply down and sent the clerk Alincha with it.

sentences.zh: 布寨要至其寨，不令見納林布祿，遣還。

translations.literal: Buzhai insisted he come to his stockade but would not let him see Nalinbulu, and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: Buzhai summoned him to his camp but refused a meeting with Nalinbulu and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 未幾，長白山所屬硃舍裡、訥殷二路引葉赫兵劫太祖所屬東界洞寨。

translations.literal: Before long the Zhusheri and Neyin routes under Changbai Mountain led Yehhe troops to raid cave stockades on the Taizu's eastern border.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Zhusheri and Neyin districts of Changbai Mountain guided Yehhe raiders against the Taizu's eastern border forts.

sentences.zh: 二十一年夏六月，扈倫四部合兵攻太祖，布寨、納林布祿為戎首，劫戶布察寨。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of summer in the twenty-first year the four Hulun tribes united to attack the Taizu; Buzhai and Nalinbulu were the war leaders and raided Hubucha stockade.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twenty-first year the four Hulun tribes joined against the Taizu. Buzhai and Nalinbulu led the host and struck Hubucha stockade.

sentences.zh: 太祖以師御之，遂侵哈達。
