translations.literal: The Taizu met them with his army and then invaded Hada.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu marched out to meet them, then turned and struck Hada.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，复益以蒙古科爾沁、席北、卦爾察三部，硃舍裡、訥殷二路，攻太祖，謂之「九姓之師」。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn they were reinforced by the Mongol Horqin, Xibei, and Guo'ercha tribes and the Zhusheri and Neyin routes in an attack on the Taizu—called the "Army of the Nine Clans."
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, the ninth month, Horqin Mongols, Xibei, Guo'ercha, Zhusheri, and Neyin joined the assault—the "Army of the Nine Clans."

sentences.zh: 太祖將出師，祀於堂子，祝曰：「我初與葉赫無釁，葉赫橫來相攻，糾集諸部，為暴於無辜，天其鑑之！」

translations.literal: When the Taizu was about to march he sacrificed at the tangse and prayed: "At first I had no quarrel with Yehhe; Yehhe came wantonly to attack, gathering tribes and doing violence to the innocent—may Heaven witness!"
translations.idiomatic: Before marching the Taizu sacrificed at the tangse and prayed: "I did no wrong to Yehhe, yet Yehhe gathered the tribes to ravage the innocent—Heaven, see this!"

sentences.zh: 又祝曰：「原敵盡垂首，我軍奮揚，人不遺鞭，馬無顛躓，惟天其助我！」

translations.literal: He prayed again: "May the enemy all hang their heads; may our army exalt; may no man drop his whip; may no horse stumble—may Heaven aid us!"
translations.idiomatic: He prayed again: "Let the foe bow their heads; let our men fight boldly; let no rider lose his whip or horse stumble—Heaven, help us!"

sentences.zh: 是時，葉赫兵萬人，哈達、烏喇、輝發三部合兵萬人，蒙古科爾沁三貝勒及席北、皆懼，太祖戒勉之。

translations.literal: At this time Yehhe had ten thousand men; Hada, Wula, and Huifa together fielded ten thousand; the three Mongol Horqin beiles and Xibei were all fearful, and the Taizu admonished and encouraged them.
translations.idiomatic: Yehhe mustered ten thousand men; Hada, Wula, and Huifa another ten thousand; the Horqin beiles and Xibei allies were all afraid, and the Taizu exhorted and heartened them.

sentences.zh: 朝發虎闌哈達，夕宿扎喀？

translations.literal: They marched from Hulan Hada at dawn and lodged at Zhaka at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: They broke camp at Hulan Hada at dawn and encamped at Zhaka by nightfall.

sentences.zh: 卦爾察三部又萬人，凡三萬人。

translations.literal: The three Guo'ercha tribes added another ten thousand—thirty thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: Guo'ercha contributed ten thousand more—thirty thousand in all.

sentences.zh: 太祖兵少，城。

translations.literal: The Taizu's army was few, yet he advanced on the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu had few troops, but he pressed on to the city.

sentences.zh: 葉赫兵方攻黑濟格城，未下。

translations.literal: The Yehhe army was attacking Heijige city and had not yet taken it.
translations.idiomatic: Yehhe was besieging Heijige and had not yet captured it.

sentences.zh: 旦日，太祖師至，面城而陣，使額亦都以百人先。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day the Taizu's army arrived, drew up facing the city, and sent Eidu ahead with a hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the Taizu came up, formed line before the city, and sent Eidu forward with a hundred men.

sentences.zh: 葉赫兵罷攻城來戰，太祖軍迎擊，斬九級，葉赫兵小卻。

translations.literal: The Yehhe troops abandoned the siege to give battle; the Taizu's army met them, beheaded nine men, and the Yehhe line gave slightly back.
translations.idiomatic: Yehhe broke off the siege to fight. The Taizu's men engaged them, took nine heads, and the Yehhe force fell back a little.

sentences.zh: 布寨、金台石及蒙古科爾沁三貝勒复並力合攻，金台石者，納林布祿弟也。

translations.literal: Buzhai, Jintaishi, and the three Mongol Horqin beiles again united to attack together; Jintaishi was Nalinbulu's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Buzhai, Jintaishi, and the three Horqin beiles joined forces again; Jintaishi was Nalinbulu's brother.

sentences.zh: 布寨將突陣，馬觸木，踣，太祖部卒吳談趨而前，伏其身刺殺之。

translations.literal: As Buzhai charged the line his horse struck a timber and fell; the Taizu's soldier Wu Tan rushed forward, leaned over him, and stabbed him dead.
translations.idiomatic: Buzhai charged the line; his horse hit a stake and threw him. Wu Tan of the Taizu's guard ran up, leaned over him, and drove a blade into him.

sentences.zh: 葉赫兵見布寨死，皆痛哭，陣遂亂。

translations.literal: Seeing Buzhai dead, the Yehhe troops all wailed; the formation fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When Buzhai fell the Yehhe ranks broke into mourning and the battle line collapsed.

sentences.zh: 九姓之師以此敗。

translations.literal: The Army of the Nine Clans was defeated for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Army of the Nine Clans was broken.

sentences.zh: 布寨死，子佈揚古嗣為貝勒。

translations.literal: When Buzhai died, his son Buyanggu succeeded as beile.
translations.idiomatic: Buzhai's son Buyanggu succeeded him as beile.

sentences.zh: 二十五年春正月，扈倫諸部同遣使行成於太祖曰：「吾等兵敗名辱，繼自今願締舊好，申之以婚媾。」

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the twenty-fifth year the Hulun tribes together sent envoys suing for peace with the Taizu, saying: "We are defeated and disgraced; from now on we wish to renew the old friendship and seal it with marriage."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-fifth year the Hulun tribes sued for peace: "We are beaten and shamed; let us restore the old friendship and bind it with marriage."

sentences.zh: 布揚古請以女弟歸太祖，金台石請以女妻太祖次子台吉代善，上許之，具禮以聘。

translations.literal: Buyanggu asked to send his younger sister to the Taizu; Jintaishi asked to give his daughter to the Taizu's second son, Taiji Daishan; the sovereign assented and sent betrothal gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Buyanggu offered his younger sister to the Taizu; Jintaishi offered his daughter to the second son Daishan. The Taizu agreed and sent betrothal gifts.

sentences.zh: 宰牛馬告天，設巵酒、塊土及肉、血、骨各一器，四國使者誓曰：「既盟之後，苟棄婚媾，背盟約，如此土，如此骨，如此血，永墜厥命！

translations.literal: They slaughtered cattle and horses to announce to Heaven, set out goblets of wine, lumps of earth, and vessels of meat, blood, and bone; envoys of the four states swore: "After this covenant, if we abandon the marriage or break the pact, then like this earth, like this bone, like this blood—may our lives fall forever!
translations.idiomatic: They sacrificed oxen and horses to Heaven and set out wine, clods of earth, meat, blood, and bone. Envoys of the four powers swore: "If we forsake this marriage or break faith, may we perish like this earth, this bone, this blood!

sentences.zh: 若始終不渝，飲此酒，食此肉，福祿永昌。」

translations.literal: If to the end we do not waver, drink this wine and eat this meat—fortune and long life everlasting."
translations.idiomatic: If we keep faith to the end, drink this wine and eat this meat—may fortune and long life endure."

sentences.zh: 太祖誓曰：「彼等踐盟則已，有或渝者，待三年不悛，吾乃討之。」

translations.literal: The Taizu swore: "If they keep the covenant, well; if any violate it, when three years pass without repentance I will punish them."
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu swore: "Let them keep the pact; if anyone breaks it and does not repent within three years, I will strike."

sentences.zh: 布揚古女弟，高皇后姪也，是時年十四。

translations.literal: Buyanggu's younger sister was the High Empress's niece; she was then fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: Buyanggu's sister was the High Empress's niece—fourteen years old at the time.

sentences.zh: 未幾，太祖遣將穆哈連侵蒙古，獲馬四十。

translations.literal: Before long the Taizu sent the general Mughaliyan to raid the Mongols and captured forty horses.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Taizu sent Mughaliyan against the Mongols; he brought back forty horses.

sentences.zh: 納林布祿邀奪其馬，執穆哈連歸於蒙古。

translations.literal: Nalinbulu intercepted and seized the horses and took Mughaliyan back into Mongol territory.
translations.idiomatic: Nalinbulu seized the horses, captured Mughaliyan, and carried him off to the Mongols.

sentences.zh: 烏喇貝勒布占泰亦背盟結納林布祿。

translations.literal: The Wula beile Butai also broke the covenant and joined Nalinbulu.
translations.idiomatic: Butai, beile of Wula, broke the pact as well and sided with Nalinbulu.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，太祖克哈達。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year the Taizu conquered Hada.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year the Taizu overthrew Hada.

sentences.zh: 以明有責言，使哈達故貝勒孟格布祿子吳爾古代還所部。

translations.literal: Because the Ming spoke rebuke, he sent Hada's former beile Menggebulu's son Wuergudai back to his department.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ming protested, he restored Menggebulu's son Wuergudai to his clan lands.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，納林布祿以兵侵之，太祖遂以吳爾古代歸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year Nalinbulu invaded him with troops; the Taizu then returned Wuergudai.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year Nalinbulu attacked; the Taizu sent Wuergudai back to Hada.

sentences.zh: 三十一年秋九月，高皇后疾篤，思見母，太祖使迎焉。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn in the thirty-first year the High Empress was gravely ill and longed to see her mother; the Taizu sent to bring her.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the thirty-first year the High Empress lay dying and wished to see her mother; the Taizu sent to fetch her.

sentences.zh: 納林布祿不許，令其僕南太來視疾，太祖數之曰：「汝葉赫諸舅無故掠我戶布察寨，又合九姓之師而來攻我，既乃自服其辜，歃血誓天爲盟誓，而又背之，許我國之女皆嫁蒙古。

translations.literal: Nalinbulu would not permit it but sent his servant Nantai to inquire after her illness; the Taizu reproached him, saying: "You Yehhe uncles raided my Hubucha stockade without cause and united the Army of the Nine Clans to attack me; then you confessed your guilt and swore a blood oath to Heaven, yet you broke it again and promised the daughters of our state to Mongols in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Nalinbulu refused and sent only his servant Nantai to visit her sickbed. The Taizu rebuked him: "Your Yehhe kinsmen plundered Hubucha without cause, sent the Nine Clans against me, then swore a blood oath—and broke it again, marrying our pledged women to Mongols.

sentences.zh: 今我國妃病篤，欲與母訣，而又不許，是終絕我也！」

translations.literal: Now my state's consort is gravely ill and wishes to bid her mother farewell, yet you again forbid it—this is to cut me off forever!"
translations.idiomatic: Now my consort is dying and only wants to see her mother once more, and you refuse—that is to sever us for good!"

sentences.zh: 既而，高皇后崩。

translations.literal: Shortly after, the High Empress died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, the High Empress died.

sentences.zh: 三十二年春正月，太祖帥師攻葉赫，克二城，曰張，曰阿氣蘭；

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the thirty-second year the Taizu led his army against Yehhe and took two cities, called Zhang and Aqilan;
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the thirty-second year the Taizu attacked Yehhe and captured two cities, Zhang and Aqilan;

sentences.zh: 取七寨，俘二千餘人而還。

translations.literal: he took seven stockades, captured more than two thousand people, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: took seven stockades, seized more than two thousand people, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，納林布祿聞輝發貝勒拜音達里使貳於太祖，太祖以是取輝發，納林布祿不能救；

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year Nalinbulu heard that the Huifa beile Bayindari was inclining to the Taizu; the Taizu on that account took Huifa, and Nalinbulu could not save it;
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year Nalinbulu learned that Bayindari of Huifa was leaning toward the Taizu. The Taizu seized Huifa and Nalinbulu could not relieve it;

sentences.zh: 而布揚古女弟受太祖聘，十六年不遣，年三十，烏喇貝勒布佔泰將強委禽焉。

translations.literal: yet Buyanggu's younger sister had received the Taizu's betrothal and for sixteen years was not sent away; she was thirty, and the Wula beile Butai was about to seize her by force.
translations.idiomatic: meanwhile Buyanggu's sister, betrothed to the Taizu for sixteen years, was still withheld—thirty years old now—and Butai of Wula meant to take her by force.

sentences.zh: 四十年，太祖討布佔泰。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year the Taizu punished Butai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year the Taizu marched against Butai.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，師再舉，遂克烏喇，布佔泰亡奔葉赫。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year the army marched again and then conquered Wula; Butai fled in defeat to Yehhe.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year he marched again, overthrew Wula, and Butai fled to Yehhe.

sentences.zh: 布揚古欲遂以女弟嫁之，布佔泰遜謝不敢娶，為別婚。

translations.literal: Buyanggu wished then to marry his younger sister to him; Butai declined with apologies and dared not take her, and arranged another marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Buyanggu would have given his sister to Butai, but Butai humbly refused and took another wife.

sentences.zh: 是時納林布祿已死，其弟金台石嗣為貝勒，與布揚古分居東、西城如故。

translations.literal: By then Nalinbulu had died; his younger brother Jintaishi succeeded as beile and dwelt with Buyanggu in the eastern and western cities as before.
translations.idiomatic: Nalinbulu was dead; his brother Jintaishi became beile and still shared the eastern and western cities with Buyanggu.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，太祖使告葉赫執布佔泰以獻，使三往，不聽。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn the Taizu sent word to Yehhe to seize Butai and hand him over; he sent three times—they would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the Taizu demanded that Yehhe surrender Butai. He asked three times; they refused.

sentences.zh: 太祖謀伐之，先期遣第七子巴布泰率所屬阿都、幹骨裡等三十餘人質於明。

translations.literal: The Taizu planned to attack; beforehand he sent his seventh son Babutai with more than thirty followers including ADu and Ganguli as hostages to the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: He prepared to attack and first sent his seventh son Babutai with ADu, Ganguli, and thirty others as hostages to the Ming.

sentences.zh: 至廣寧，謁巡撫都御史張濤，請敕葉赫遣布佔泰，濤以聞，神宗下部議，以為質子真偽莫可辨，拒勿納。

translations.literal: At Guangning he visited the censor-in-chief Zhang Tao and asked an order that Yehhe send Butai; Tao reported upward; Emperor Shenzong referred it to the ministries, who held that the hostages' authenticity could not be verified and refused to accept them.
translations.idiomatic: At Guangning he saw Censor Zhang Tao and asked the court to order Yehhe to surrender Butai. Tao reported to Beijing; Shenzong referred the matter to the ministries, which doubted the hostages were genuine and turned them away.

sentences.zh: 太祖乃以四萬人會蒙古喀爾喀貝勒介賽伐葉赫。

translations.literal: The Taizu then united forty thousand men with the Mongol Khalkha beile Jiesai to attack Yehhe.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu then marched forty thousand men, joined by the Khalkha beile Jiesai, against Yehhe.

sentences.zh: 會有逋卒洩師期，葉赫收張、吉當阿二路民堡。

translations.literal: A deserter leaked the campaign date; Yehhe gathered the civilian forts of the Zhang and Jidang'a routes.
translations.idiomatic: A runaway revealed the schedule; Yehhe pulled the people of the Zhang and Jidang'a routes into the forts.

sentences.zh: 太祖圍兀蘇城，城長山談、扈石木降，太祖飲以金，

translations.literal: The Taizu besieged Wusu city; the fort chiefs Shantan and Husumu surrendered; the Taizu entertained them with a gold cup.
translations.idiomatic: He besieged Wusu; the commanders Shantan and Husumu submitted, and the Taizu honored them with a gold goblet.

sentences.zh: 賜冠服；

translations.literal: and bestowed caps and robes;
translations.idiomatic: and gave them caps and robes;

sentences.zh: 遂略張、吉當阿、呀哈、黑兒蘇、何敦、克布齊賚、俄吉岱七城，下十九寨，盡焚其廬舍儲峙，以兀蘇城降民三百戶還。

translations.literal: he then overran the seven cities Zhang, Jidang'a, Yaha, Heiersu, Hedun, Kebuqizai, and Ejidai, took nineteen stockades, burned all lodges and stored grain, and returned with three hundred households of people who had surrendered at Wusu city.
translations.idiomatic: then took seven cities—Zhang, Jidang'a, Yaha, Heiersu, Hedun, Kebuqizai, and Ejidai—plus nineteen stockades, burned their houses and stores, and withdrew with three hundred households from surrendered Wusu.

sentences.zh: 葉赫愬於明，以兵援，遇介賽，戰勝，遂遣使讓太祖，令游擊馬時柟、周大岐率兵千，挾火器，戍葉赫。

translations.literal: Yehhe complained to the Ming; the Ming sent troops to aid them, met Jiesai, and won the battle; then they sent an envoy to reproach the Taizu and ordered the patrol officers Ma Shinan and Zhou Daqi to lead a thousand men with firearms to garrison Yehhe.
translations.idiomatic: Yehhe appealed to the Ming; Ming reinforcements met Jiesai and won. Then they rebuked the Taizu and posted Patrol Officers Ma Shinan and Zhou Daqi with a thousand musketeers to guard Yehhe.

sentences.zh: 太祖至撫順，投書游擊李永芳，申言：「侵葉赫，以葉赫背盟，女已字，悔不遣，又匿布佔泰；

translations.literal: The Taizu reached Fushun and sent a letter to Patrol Officer Li Yongfang, stating: "I invade Yehhe because Yehhe broke the covenant—the girl was already betrothed yet they regretted and would not send her, and they also hid Butai;
translations.idiomatic: At Fushun the Taizu wrote to Patrol Officer Li Yongfang: "I strike Yehhe because it broke faith—the girl was pledged and withheld, and Butai was sheltered there;

sentences.zh: 故與明無怨，何遽欲相侵？」

translations.literal: thus I bear the Ming no grudge—why do you suddenly wish to invade each other?"
translations.idiomatic: I have no quarrel with the Ming—why turn on me now?"

sentences.zh: 遂引師還。

translations.literal: He then withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: Then he marched home.

sentences.zh: 金台石有女，育於其兄納林布祿，嫁介賽。

translations.literal: Jintaishi had a daughter who had been raised at her elder brother Nalinbulu's and was married to Jiesai.
translations.idiomatic: Jintaishi had a daughter, raised in Nalinbulu's household, who was married to Jiesai.

sentences.zh: 金台石既為貝勒，殺納林布祿妻，介賽假辭為外姑復仇，覬得布揚古女弟以​​解。

translations.literal: After Jintaishi became beile he killed Nalinbulu's wife; Jiesai used the pretext of avenging his mother-in-law and coveted obtaining Buyanggu's younger sister to settle the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When Jintaishi became beile he killed Nalinbulu's wife. Jiesai claimed revenge for his mother-in-law and sought Buyanggu's sister to end the feud.

sentences.zh: 布揚古女弟誓死不原行。

translations.literal: Buyanggu's younger sister vowed she would rather die than go.
translations.idiomatic: Buyanggu's sister swore she would die before she went.

sentences.zh: 介賽治兵攻葉赫。

translations.literal: Jiesai marshaled troops and attacked Yehhe.
translations.idiomatic: Jiesai raised an army and attacked Yehhe.

sentences.zh: 既而喀爾喀貝勒巴哈達爾漢為其子莽古爾代請婚，布揚古將許之。

translations.literal: Before long the Khalkha beile Bahadahan requested marriage for his son Manggu'erdai; Buyanggu was about to consent.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Khalkha beile Bahadahan asked his son Manggu'erdai for Buyanggu's sister; Buyanggu was ready to agree.

sentences.zh: 明邊吏諭布揚古，姑留此女，毋使葉赫。

translations.literal: Ming border officials instructed Buyanggu to keep the girl for the time being and not let her go to Yehhe.
translations.idiomatic: Ming border officials told Buyanggu to hold the girl and not let Yehhe have her.

sentences.zh: 四十三年夏？

translations.literal: Summer of the forty-third year
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the forty-third year

sentences.zh: 縻；

translations.literal: she was detained;
translations.idiomatic: she was held;

sentences.zh: 而以兵分屯開原、撫順及鎮北堡為犄角，？

translations.literal: and troops were posted separately at Kaiyuan, Fushun, and Zhenbei fort as supporting horns— the Taizu and Jiesai's hopes were utterly cut off.
translations.idiomatic: and Ming troops were stationed at Kaiyuan, Fushun, and Zhenbei fort in mutual support; until the Taizu and Jiesai despaired completely.

sentences.zh: 太祖及介賽望絕，冀相五月，布揚古遂以其女弟許莽古爾代，秋七月婚焉。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fifth month Buyanggu then betrothed his younger sister to Manggu'erdai; in the seventh month of autumn the marriage was performed.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fifth month Buyanggu gave his sister to Manggu'erdai; the wedding followed in the seventh month.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞，諸貝勒皆怒，請討葉赫，不許。

translations.literal: When the Taizu heard, all the beiles were angry and asked to punish Yehhe—not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taizu heard, his beiles were furious and begged to strike Yehhe; he refused.

sentences.zh: 請侵明，又不許，且曰：「此女生不祥，哈達、輝發、烏喇三部以此女構怨，相繼覆亡。

translations.literal: They asked to invade the Ming; again he did not permit it, and said: "This girl is unlucky; Hada, Huifa, and Wula were ruined because of her and the enmity she stirred.
translations.idiomatic: They urged an attack on the Ming; again he refused, saying: "This woman brings ill fortune. Hada, Huifa, and Wula were destroyed over her.

sentences.zh: 今明助葉赫，不與我而與蒙古，殆天欲亡葉赫，以激其怒也。

translations.literal: Now the Ming aids Yehhe and gives her not to me but to the Mongols—perhaps Heaven wishes to destroy Yehhe and stir their wrath.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming backs Yehhe and gives her to the Mongols, not to us—perhaps Heaven means to ruin Yehhe and goad them to ruin.

sentences.zh: 我知此女流禍將盡，死不遠矣。」

translations.literal: I know this girl's flowing calamity is nearly spent—her death is not far."
translations.idiomatic: I know her curse is almost done—she will not live long."

sentences.zh: 布揚古女弟嫁莽古爾代未一年而死，死時年蓋三十四，明所謂「北關老女」者也。

translations.literal: Buyanggu's younger sister, married to Manggu'erdai less than a year, died; at death she was about thirty-four—the person the Ming called the "Old Maid of the North Pass."
translations.idiomatic: Buyanggu's sister had been wed to Manggu'erdai less than a year when she died, aged about thirty-four—the Ming knew her as the Old Maid of the North Pass.

sentences.zh: 是歲為太祖天命元年。

translations.literal: That year was the first year of the Taizu's Tianming reign.
translations.idiomatic: That year was the first year of Taizu's Tianming era.

sentences.zh: 太祖既稱帝建國，始用兵於明。

translations.literal: After the Taizu had declared himself emperor and founded the state, he first took up arms against the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Taizu had proclaimed himself emperor and founded his state, he turned his armies against the Ming.

sentences.zh: 三年，攻撫順、清河。

translations.literal: In the third year he attacked Fushun and Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he attacked Fushun and Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 明經略侍郎楊鎬使諭葉赫發兵撓太祖。

translations.literal: Ming frontier commissioner Yang Gao sent orders instructing Yehhe to raise troops and harass the Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Ming frontier commissioner Yang Gao ordered Yehhe to raise troops and harry the Taizu.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，金台石子德爾格勒侵太祖，克一寨，俘四百七人，斬八十四級。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn Jintaishi's son Delgeler raided the Taizu, captured one stockade, took four hundred seven prisoners, and severed eighty-four heads.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, in the ninth month, Jintaishi's son Delgeler struck the Taizu, took a stockade, captured four hundred seven people, and cut off eighty-four heads.

sentences.zh: 明賜以白金二千兩、採緞表里二十。

translations.literal: The Ming rewarded him with two thousand taels of white silver and twenty rolls of figured silk, inner and outer.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming rewarded him with two thousand taels of silver and twenty bolts of figured silk.

sentences.zh: 四年春正月，太祖謀報之，使大貝勒代善以兵五千戍札喀關阻明師，而躬督兵伐葉赫。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the fourth year the Taizu planned reprisal, sent the Great Beile Daishan with five thousand men to garrison Zhaka Pass and block Ming troops, and personally led an army against Yehhe.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year the Taizu planned his reply: he posted the Great Beile Daishan with five thousand men at Zhaka Pass to block Ming forces while he led the main army against Yehhe.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，入其境，經克亦特城、粘罕寨，至葉赫城東十里，克大小屯寨二十餘。

translations.literal: On xinmao day he entered their territory, passed Keyite City and Zhanhan Stockade, reached a point ten li east of Yehhe City, and captured more than twenty large and small fortified hamlets.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao day he crossed their border, passed Keyite and Zhanhan, came within ten li of Yehhe City, and took more than twenty fortified hamlets.

sentences.zh: 葉赫乞援於明，明開原總兵馬林以師至，合城兵而出，見太祖兵盛，不敢擊。

translations.literal: Yehhe begged aid from the Ming; Ming Kaiyuan commander Ma Lin arrived with his army, joined the city troops and marched out, but seeing the Taizu's forces strong, dared not attack.
translations.idiomatic: Yehhe appealed to the Ming; Kaiyuan commander Ma Lin marched out with the city garrison, saw how strong the Taizu's army was, and dared not give battle.

sentences.zh: 太祖亦引還。

translations.literal: The Taizu also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 二月，楊鎬大舉伐太祖，使都司竇永澄徵兵於葉赫，葉赫以二千人應。

translations.literal: In the second month Yang Gao launched a major campaign against the Taizu, had Commissioner Dou Yongcheng levy troops from Yehhe, and Yehhe sent two thousand men in response.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Yang Gao mounted a major offensive against the Taizu; Commissioner Dou Yongcheng was sent to levy troops from Yehhe, which furnished two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 至三岔北，明師覆，永澄死之。

translations.literal: At the north of Sancha the Ming army was destroyed and Yongcheng died in the rout.
translations.idiomatic: North of Sancha the Ming army was shattered; Yongcheng died in the rout.

sentences.zh: 太祖謀使所屬詐降於金台石，金台石不應。

translations.literal: The Taizu plotted to have his followers feign surrender to Jintaishi; Jintaishi would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu tried to have his men feign surrender to Jintaishi; Jintaishi refused.

sentences.zh: 六月，太祖攻開原，葉赫復以二千人援，至則開原已下。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the Taizu attacked Kaiyuan; Yehhe again sent two thousand as reinforcements, but when they arrived Kaiyuan had already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the Taizu attacked Kaiyuan; Yehhe sent two thousand reinforcements, but by the time they arrived Kaiyuan had already fallen.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，經略侍郎熊廷弼初視事，葉赫使期復開原，廷弼厚賚之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn Frontier Commissioner Xiong Tingbi had just taken office; Yehhe envoys hoped to recover Kaiyuan, and Tingbi richly rewarded them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Xiong Tingbi had just assumed office as frontier commissioner; Yehhe envoys still hoped to win back Kaiyuan, and he rewarded them generously.

sentences.zh: 太祖惎葉赫，八月，大舉伐之。

translations.literal: The Taizu harbored enmity toward Yehhe; in the eighth month he launched a major campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu nursed a grudge against Yehhe; that eighth month he mounted a full-scale invasion.

sentences.zh: 己巳，師出，聲言向瀋陽，以綴明師。

translations.literal: On jisi day the army set out, proclaiming it was heading for Shenyang to detain Ming forces.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi day the army marched, announcing it was bound for Shenyang to pin down Ming troops.

sentences.zh: 壬申，至葉赫城下，太祖攻金台石東城，而命諸貝勒馳向西城取布揚古。

translations.literal: On renshen day they reached below Yehhe City; the Taizu attacked Jintaishi's eastern city and ordered the beiles to gallop west and take Buyanggu.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day they came beneath Yehhe City; the Taizu assaulted Jintaishi's eastern citadel while ordering his beiles to ride west and seize Buyanggu.

sentences.zh: 布揚古與其弟布爾杭古以城兵出西郭，陟岡，鳴角而噪，望太祖軍盛，斂兵入。

translations.literal: Buyanggu and his brother Burianggugu led city troops out the western gate, climbed a hill, blew horns and shouted, but seeing the Taizu's army strong, drew their troops back in.
translations.idiomatic: Buyanggu and his brother Burianggugu marched out the west gate with the garrison, climbed a hill, blew horns and shouted—but seeing the Taizu's strength, they pulled back inside.

sentences.zh: 諸貝勒遂督軍合圍。

translations.literal: The beiles then directed the troops in a joint encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: The beiles then closed the ring around the city.

sentences.zh: 太祖圍東城，入其郛，布攻具，呼金台石降，不聽，曰：「吾非明兵比，等丈夫也，肯束手降乎？

translations.literal: The Taizu besieged the eastern city, entered its outer ramparts, deployed siege equipment, and called on Jintaishi to surrender. Jintaishi would not heed him and said: "I am not like Ming soldiers—you are men of standing; would I willingly submit bound hand and foot?
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu invested the eastern city, entered the outer works, set siege engines, and called on Jintaishi to yield. Jintaishi refused: "I am no Ming soldier—you are men of honor; do you think I would surrender with hands bound?

sentences.zh: 寧戰而死耳。」

translations.literal: I would rather die fighting."
translations.idiomatic: I would rather die fighting."

sentences.zh: 太祖麾兵攻城，兩軍矢交發，太祖軍擁楯陟山麓，將穴城，城上下木石，擲火器。

translations.literal: The Taizu waved his troops to assault the city; arrows flew from both sides. The Taizu's men pressed forward behind shields up the foothills, about to mine the wall; from above they cast timber, stone, and fire weapons.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu ordered the assault; arrows crossed in both directions. His men pressed up the slope behind shields to undermine the wall while defenders hurled timber, stone, and fire weapons from above.

sentences.zh: 太祖軍冒進，穴城，城圮，師入，城兵迎戰，敗潰，皆散​​走。

translations.literal: The Taizu's army pressed on, mined the wall, the wall collapsed, troops entered; city soldiers met them in battle, were defeated and scattered in flight.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu's men pressed on, undermined the wall until it gave way, and poured in; the garrison met them, broke, and fled in disorder.

sentences.zh: 太祖使執幟約軍士毋妄殺，執黃蓋，令降者免死，城民皆請降。

translations.literal: The Taizu had banner-bearers instruct the soldiers not to kill indiscriminately; they held up yellow canopies, promising death exemption to those who surrendered, and the townspeople all asked to submit.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu sent men with banners to forbid indiscriminate killing; yellow canopies were raised promising life to those who surrendered, and the townspeople all submitted.

sentences.zh: 金台石以其孥登台，太祖軍就圍之，命之下。

translations.literal: Jintaishi took his wife and children up onto a tower; the Taizu's army closed around it and ordered them down.
translations.idiomatic: Jintaishi took his family up onto a tower; the Taizu's troops surrounded it and ordered them down.

sentences.zh: 金台石求見四貝勒盟而後下，四貝勒為太宗，高皇后所出，金台石甥也。

translations.literal: Jintaishi asked to see the Fourth Beile and covenant before coming down; the Fourth Beile was Huang Taiji, born of the High Empress, Jintaishi's nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Jintaishi asked to see the Fourth Beile and swear a pact before descending; the Fourth Beile was Huang Taiji, son of the High Empress and Jintaishi's nephew.

sentences.zh: 四貝勒方攻西城，太祖召之至，使見金台石。

translations.literal: The Fourth Beile was then attacking the western city; the Taizu summoned him and had him see Jintaishi.
translations.idiomatic: The Fourth Beile was still assaulting the western city; the Taizu summoned him and brought him before Jintaishi.

sentences.zh: 金台石曰：「我未嘗見我甥，真偽烏能辨？」

translations.literal: Jintaishi said: "I have never seen my nephew—how could I tell true from false?"
translations.idiomatic: Jintaishi said: "I have never laid eyes on my nephew—how can I know whether this is truly he?"

sentences.zh: 費英東、達爾哈在側，曰：「汝視常人中有奇偉如四貝勒者乎？

translations.literal: Feiyingdong and Daihar, standing by, said: "Do you see among ordinary men anyone as remarkably imposing as the Fourth Beile?
translations.idiomatic: Feiyingdong and Daihar, standing beside him, said: "Do you see among common men anyone as striking as the Fourth Beile?

sentences.zh: 且曩與汝通好時，嘗以媼​​往乳汝子德爾格勒，盍使媼辨之！」

translations.literal: Moreover, when we were on good terms we once sent a wet nurse to suckle your son Delgeler—why not have the nurse identify him!"
translations.idiomatic: When we were on friendly terms we sent a nurse to suckle your son Delgeler—let the nurse recognize him!"

sentences.zh: 金台石曰：「何用媼為也！

translations.literal: Jintaishi said: "What need of a nurse!
translations.idiomatic: Jintaishi said: "What need of a nurse!

sentences.zh: 觀汝輩辭色，特誘我下殺我耳。

translations.literal: Judging by your tone, you mean only to lure me down and kill me.
translations.idiomatic: Your manner shows you mean only to lure me down and kill me.

sentences.zh: 我石城鐵門既為汝破，縱再戰，安能勝？

translations.literal: My stone walls and iron gates you have already broken; even if I fought again, how could I win?
translations.idiomatic: You have already broken my stone walls and iron gates; even if I fought again, how could I prevail?

sentences.zh: 特我祖父世分土於斯，我生於斯，長於斯，則死於斯可已。」

translations.literal: Only that my ancestors for generations held their fief here—I was born here, grew up here; to die here is enough."
translations.idiomatic: My ancestors held this land for generations; I was born here and grew up here—to die here is enough."

sentences.zh: 四貝勒勸之力，金台石使阿爾塔石先見太祖，太祖復令諭降。

translations.literal: The Fourth Beile urged him earnestly; Jintaishi sent Altashi first to see the Taizu; the Taizu again ordered him to summon surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Fourth Beile pressed him hard; Jintaishi sent Altashi first to the Taizu, who again sent word demanding surrender.

sentences.zh: 金台石又求見其子德爾格勒，德爾格勒至，金台石終不下。

translations.literal: Jintaishi again asked to see his son Delgeler; when Delgeler came, Jintaishi still would not come down.
translations.idiomatic: Jintaishi asked again to see his son Delgeler; Delgeler came, yet Jintaishi still would not descend.

sentences.zh: 四貝勒將縛德爾格勒，德爾格勒曰：「我年三十六，乃今日死耶！

translations.literal: The Fourth Beile was about to bind Delgeler; Delgeler said: "I am thirty-six—am I to die only today!
translations.idiomatic: The Fourth Beile was about to bind Delgeler; Delgeler cried: "I am thirty-six—must I die only today!

sentences.zh: 殺可也，何縛焉？」

translations.literal: Kill me if you will—why bind me?"
translations.idiomatic: Kill me if you must—why bind me?"

sentences.zh: 四貝勒以德爾格勒見太祖，太祖撤所食食之，命四貝勒與共食。

translations.literal: The Fourth Beile brought Delgeler before the Taizu; the Taizu set aside his own food and fed him, and ordered the Fourth Beile to eat with him.
translations.idiomatic: The Fourth Beile presented Delgeler to the Taizu, who shared his own meal with him and bade the Fourth Beile eat beside him.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「爾兄也，善遇之！」

translations.literal: And said: "He is your elder brother—treat him well!"
translations.idiomatic: He added: "He is your brother—see that he is well treated!"

sentences.zh: 金台石妻將其幼子下，金台石引弓，其從者復甲。

translations.literal: Jintaishi's wife was bringing down their young son; Jintaishi drew his bow and his followers donned armor again.
translations.idiomatic: Jintaishi's wife was lowering their young son; Jintaishi strung his bow and his followers armed themselves again.

sentences.zh: 太祖軍進毀台，金台石縱火，屋宇皆燼。

translations.literal: The Taizu's army advanced and destroyed the tower; Jintaishi set fire and the buildings were all reduced to ash.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu's troops pressed forward and wrecked the tower; Jintaishi set it ablaze and the buildings burned to ash.

sentences.zh: 太祖諸將謂金台石且死，軍退。

translations.literal: The Taizu's generals thought Jintaishi must be dead and the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu's generals assumed Jintaishi was dead and drew the army back.

sentences.zh: 火燼，金台石潛下，為太祖軍所獲，縊殺之。

translations.literal: When the embers cooled, Jintaishi stole down and was seized by the Taizu's army and strangled.
translations.idiomatic: When the fire died, Jintaishi slipped down, was seized by the Taizu's men, and strangled.

sentences.zh: 諸貝勒圍西城，布揚古聞東城破，與布爾杭古使請降，並請盟無死。

translations.literal: The beiles besieged the western city; Buyanggu heard the eastern city had fallen; he and Burianggugu sent to beg surrender and also asked for covenant that they would not be killed.
translations.idiomatic: The beiles invested the western city; hearing the east had fallen, Buyanggu and Burianggugu sued for surrender and begged a sworn pledge that their lives would be spared.

sentences.zh: 大貝勒曰：「汝輩畏死，盍以汝母先，汝母我外姑也，我寧能殺之？」

translations.literal: The Great Beile said: "You fear death—why not send your mother first? She is my mother's sister; how could I kill her?"
translations.idiomatic: The Great Beile said: "You fear death—send your mother first. She is my aunt; would I kill her?"

sentences.zh: 布揚古母至軍，大貝勒以刀劃酒，誓，飲其半，使送布揚古、布爾杭古飲其半，乃降。

translations.literal: Buyanggu's mother came to the army; the Great Beile scored wine with a knife, swore, drank half, and had it sent for Buyanggu and Burianggugu to drink the other half; then they surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Buyanggu's mother came to camp; the Great Beile cut wine with a knife, swore, drank half, and sent the rest for Buyanggu and Burianggugu to drink before they yielded.

sentences.zh: 大貝勒以布揚古見太祖，布揚古行復勒馬，大貝勒挽其轡，命毋沮。

translations.literal: The Great Beile brought Buyanggu to see the Taizu; Buyanggu walked, then checked his horse again; the Great Beile seized his bridle and ordered him not to hesitate.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Beile led Buyanggu before the Taizu; Buyanggu walked, then checked his horse; the Great Beile took his bridle and told him not to hang back.

sentences.zh: 見太祖，布揚古以一膝跪，不拜而起。

translations.literal: When he saw the Taizu, Buyanggu knelt on one knee, did not bow, and rose.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Taizu, Buyanggu dropped to one knee, refused to bow, and stood again.

sentences.zh: 太祖取金？

translations.literal: The Taizu took a gold goblet.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu took up a gold goblet.

sentences.zh: 授之，布揚古復以一膝跪，酒不竟飲，不拜而起。

translations.literal: When it was offered him, Buyanggu again knelt on one knee, did not finish the wine, did not bow, and rose.
translations.idiomatic: When it was offered, Buyanggu again knelt on one knee, left the wine unfinished, refused to bow, and rose.

sentences.zh: 太祖命大貝勒引去，以其懟也，即夕亦縊殺之。

translations.literal: The Taizu ordered the Great Beile to lead him away; because of his defiance, that same evening he too was strangled.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu ordered the Great Beile to lead him away; for his insolence he was strangled that same night.

sentences.zh: 貸布爾杭古。

translations.literal: Burianggugu was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Burianggugu was spared.

sentences.zh: 攻殺明游擊馬時楠戍兵，殲焉。

translations.literal: They attacked and destroyed Ming patrol commander Ma Shinan's garrison troops, annihilating them.
translations.idiomatic: They attacked and wiped out the garrison of Ming patrol commander Ma Shinan.

sentences.zh: 楊鎬聞警，使總兵李如楨自撫順出，張疑兵為葉赫聲援，得十餘級而退。

translations.literal: Yang Gao heard the alarm and sent Commander Li Ruzhen out from Fushun with a feigned force as a diversion for Yehhe; he took a dozen heads and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gao heard the alarm and sent Commander Li Ruzhen from Fushun with a diversionary force toward Yehhe; he took a dozen heads and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 神宗命給事中姚宗文行邊，求葉赫子孫，德爾格勒有女子子二，嫁蒙古，各賜白金二千。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong ordered Supervisor Yao Zongwen to tour the frontier and seek descendants of Yehhe; Delgeler had two daughters and sons, married to Mongols, and each was granted two thousand taels of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong sent Supervisor Yao Zongwen to the frontier to seek survivors of Yehhe; Delgeler had two daughters and sons who had married Mongols, and each received two thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 明臣請為金台石、布揚古立廟，又以哈達餘裔王世忠為金台石妻至​​，授游擊，將以風諸部，然葉赫遂亡。

translations.literal: Ming officials asked to erect temples for Jintaishi and Buyanggu, and also appointed Wang Shizhong, a descendant of Hada, as escort for Jintaishi's wife, with the rank of patrol officer, intending thereby to sway the tribes; yet Yehhe was finally extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Ming officials proposed temples for Jintaishi and Buyanggu and made Wang Shizhong, a Hada descendant, escort Jintaishi's widow with the rank of patrol officer, hoping to sway the tribes—but Yehhe was gone.

sentences.zh: 太祖以德爾格勒歸，旗制定，隸滿洲正黃旗，授三等副將。

translations.literal: The Taizu brought Delgeler into his service; when the banners were fixed, he was assigned to the Plain Yellow Banner of the Manchu and given the rank of third-class deputy general.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu took Delgeler into service; when the Eight Banners were set, he was placed in the Plain Yellow Banner and made a third-class deputy general.

sentences.zh: 太宗天聰三年，改三等梅勒章京，卒，八年，子南楮嗣。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huang Taiji's Tiancong reign he was changed to third-class meile janggin; he died; in the eighth year his son Nanchu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Huang Taiji's Tiancong reign he was made third-class meile janggin; he died, and in the eighth year his son Nanchu inherited the post.

sentences.zh: 十年，察哈爾林丹汗殂，所部內亂，太宗遣貝勒多爾袞帥師略地。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Lindan Khan of Chakhar died; his following fell into disorder; Huang Taiji sent Beile Dorgon at the head of an army to raid their lands.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Lindan Khan of Chakhar died and his people fell into turmoil; Huang Taiji sent Beile Dorgon to raid their territory.

sentences.zh: 林丹汗福金號蘇泰太后，南楮女兄也，因使南楮諭降。

translations.literal: Lindan Khan's fujin was styled Empress Dowager Suitai, Nanchu's elder sister; he therefore sent Nanchu to urge surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Lindan Khan's consort was styled Empress Dowager Suitai, Nanchu's elder sister; Huang Taiji sent Nanchu to persuade her to submit.

sentences.zh: 南楮至其帳，呼其人出，語之曰：「爾福金蘇泰太后之弟南楮至矣！」

translations.literal: Nanchu reached their camp, called the people out, and said to them: "Your fujin Empress Dowager Suitai's younger brother Nanchu has come!"
translations.idiomatic: Nanchu came to their camp, called someone out, and said: "Empress Dowager Suitai's brother Nanchu is here!"

sentences.zh: 其人入告，蘇泰太后大驚，使故葉赫部來媵者視之，信。

translations.literal: The man went in to report; Empress Dowager Suitai was greatly startled and sent a former serving woman from Yehhe who had come as a bride-attendant to look; it was true.
translations.idiomatic: The man went in to tell her; Empress Dowager Suitai was astonished and sent a former Yehhe woman who had come as her attendant to look—and it was true.

sentences.zh: 蘇泰太后號而出，與南楮相抱持，遂使其子額哲出降。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Suitai wailed as she came out, embraced Nanchu, and then had her son Eje come out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Suitai came out wailing, embraced Nanchu, and then sent her son Eje out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 南楮旋以罪奪爵，復以南楮弟索爾和嗣。

translations.literal: Nanchu was soon stripped of his rank for a crime, and Nanchu's younger brother Suoerhe succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Nanchu was soon stripped of his rank for an offense, and his younger brother Suoerhe inherited.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，改二等男。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qianlong reign it was changed to second-class baron.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianlong reign the title was raised to second-class baron.

sentences.zh: 布爾杭古分隸正紅旗，亦授三等副將。

translations.literal: Burianggugu was assigned to the Plain Red Banner and also made third-class deputy general.
translations.idiomatic: Burianggugu was placed in the Plain Red Banner and likewise made third-class deputy general.

sentences.zh: 再傳，坐事，奪世職。

translations.literal: After two generations, for an offense, the hereditary office was revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Two generations later, for an offense, the hereditary rank was forfeited.

sentences.zh: 布佔泰，烏喇部長，太祖婿也。

translations.literal: Butai was chieftain of the Wula tribe and son-in-law to the Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Butai was chief of Wula and the Taizu's son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 烏喇亦扈倫四部之一，與哈達同祖納齊卜祿。

translations.literal: Wula was also one of the four Hulun tribes, sharing ancestor Nashibolu with Hada.
translations.idiomatic: Wula was one of the four Hulun tribes and shared ancestor Nashibolu with Hada.

sentences.zh: 納齊卜祿五傳至克什納、古對硃顏兄弟。

translations.literal: Five generations from Nashibolu came the brothers Keshina and Guduizhuyan.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations from Nashibolu came the brothers Keshina and Guduizhuyan.

sentences.zh: 克什納之後為哈達部。

translations.literal: Keshina's descendants became the Hada tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Keshina's line became the Hada tribe.

sentences.zh: 古對硃顏生太蘭，太蘭生布顏。

translations.literal: Guduizhuyan begot Tailan, and Tailan begot Buyan.
translations.idiomatic: Guduizhuyan fathered Tailan, and Tailan fathered Buyan.

sentences.zh: 布顏收附近諸部，築城洪尼，濱烏喇河，因號烏喇，為貝勒。

translations.literal: Buyan gathered nearby tribes, built Hongni City on the Wula River, and from that took the name Wula, becoming beile.
translations.idiomatic: Buyan absorbed neighboring tribes, built Hongni on the Wula River, took the name Wula from the river, and became beile.

sentences.zh: 布顏子二：布干、博克多。

translations.literal: Buyan had two sons: Bugan and Bokeduo.
translations.idiomatic: Buyan had two sons: Bugan and Bokeduo.

sentences.zh: 布顏死，布干嗣為部長。

translations.literal: When Buyan died, Bugan succeeded as chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: When Buyan died, Bugan succeeded as chief.

sentences.zh: 布干子二：滿泰、布佔泰。

translations.literal: Bugan had two sons: Mantai and Butai.
translations.idiomatic: Bugan had two sons: Mantai and Butai.

sentences.zh: 布干死，滿泰嗣為部長。

translations.literal: When Bugan died, Mantai succeeded as chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: When Bugan died, Mantai became chief.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二十一年夏六月，葉赫糾扈倫諸部侵太祖，滿泰以所部從。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of summer of the twenty-first year of Wanli, Yehhe rallied the Hulun tribes to invade the Taizu, and Mantai followed with his following.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Wanli 21, Yehhe rallied the Hulun tribes against the Taizu, and Mantai marched with his people.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，葉赫再糾扈倫諸部，及蒙古科爾沁所部，及滿洲長白山所屬，大舉分道侵太祖。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn Yehhe again rallied the Hulun tribes, the Mongol Kerqin following, and those subject to Changbaishan in Manchuria, launching a major invasion against the Taizu by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, in the ninth month, Yehhe again united the Hulun tribes with the Kerqin Mongols and the Changbaishan peoples in a great multi-pronged attack on the Taizu.

sentences.zh: 滿泰使布佔泰以所部從，與哈達貝勒孟格布祿、輝發貝勒拜音達里合軍萬人。

translations.literal: Mantai had Butai follow with his following; together with Hada Beile Menggebulu and Huifa Beile Bayindari they united an army of ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Mantai sent Butai with his following; with Hada Beile Menggebulu and Huifa Beile Bayindari they mustered ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 戰敗，葉赫貝勒布寨死於陣，科爾沁貝勒明安單騎走。

translations.literal: They were defeated; Yehhe Beile Buzhai died on the field, and Kerqin Beile Ming'an fled alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: They were beaten; Yehhe Beile Buzhai fell in battle, and Kerqin Beile Ming'an fled alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 戰之明日，卒有得布佔泰者，縛以見太祖，曰：「我獲俘，將殺之。

translations.literal: On the day after the battle a soldier captured Butai, bound him, and brought him before the Taizu, saying: "I took a prisoner and was about to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The day after the battle a soldier seized Butai, bound him, and brought him to the Taizu, saying: "I took this captive and was about to kill him.

sentences.zh: 俘大呼勿殺，原自贖。

translations.literal: The prisoner shouted not to kill him and offered to ransom himself.
translations.idiomatic: The captive cried out not to kill him and offered ransom.

sentences.zh: 因縛以來見。」

translations.literal: So he bound him and brought him to be seen."
translations.idiomatic: So he bound him and brought him in."

sentences.zh: 跽太祖前，太祖問誰何，對曰：「烏喇貝勒滿泰弟布佔泰也，生死惟貝勒命。」

translations.literal: Kneeling before the Taizu, when the Taizu asked who he was, he answered: "I am Wula Beile Mantai's younger brother Butai; life and death are at the beile's command."
translations.idiomatic: He knelt before the Taizu, who asked who he was. He answered: "I am Butai, younger brother of Wula Beile Mantai—my life is in your hands."

sentences.zh: 叩首不已。

translations.literal: He kowtowed without cease.
translations.idiomatic: He kowtowed again and again.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「汝輩合九部兵為暴於無辜，天實厭之。

translations.literal: The Taizu said: "You joined the nine tribes' armies in violence against the innocent—Heaven truly abhors it.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu said: "You united nine tribes to ravage the innocent—Heaven itself has turned against you.

sentences.zh: 昨陣斬布寨，彼時獲汝，汝死決矣！

translations.literal: Yesterday on the field Buzhai was beheaded; had you been taken then, your death was certain!
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday Buzhai was cut down on the field; had we taken you then, you would surely have died!

sentences.zh: 今見汝，何忍殺？

translations.literal: Now that I see you, how could I bear to kill you?
translations.idiomatic: Now that I see you face to face, how could I bear to kill you?

sentences.zh: 語有之曰：'生人勝殺人，與人勝取人。

translations.literal: The saying has it: 'To spare a life is better than to take a life; to give a man is better than to seize a man.
translations.idiomatic: As the saying goes: 'To spare a life is better than to take one; to give a man is better than to seize one.

sentences.zh: '」遂解其縛，與以猞猁猻裘，撫育之。

translations.literal: '" He then loosed his bonds, gave him a lynx-fur coat, and nurtured him.
translations.idiomatic: '" He untied him, gave him a lynx-fur robe, and kept him in his care.

sentences.zh: 居三年，二十四年秋七月，遣還所部，使圖爾坤黃占、博爾焜蜚揚佔護行。

translations.literal: After three years, in the seventh month of autumn of the twenty-fourth year, he was sent back to his tribe, with Tuerkun Huangzhan and Bo'erkun Feiyangzhan to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: After three years, in the seventh month of the twenty-fourth year, he was sent home with Tuerkun Huangzhan and Bo'erkun Feiyangzhan as escorts.

sentences.zh: 未至，滿泰及其子淫於所部，皆見殺。

translations.literal: Before they arrived, Mantai and his son committed lewdness in the tribe and were both killed.
translations.idiomatic: Before they arrived, Mantai and his son had debauched women of the tribe and were both slain.

sentences.zh: 布佔泰至，滿泰有叔興尼牙，將殺而奪其地，二使者嚴護之，興尼牙謀不行，乃出奔葉赫，卒定布佔泰而還。

translations.literal: When Butai arrived, Mantai had an uncle Xingniya who meant to kill him and seize his lands; the two envoys guarded him strictly, Xingniya's plot failed, he fled to Yehhe, and at last Butai was established and they returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Butai arrived, Mantai's uncle Xingniya tried to kill him and seize his domain; the two envoys guarded him closely, Xingniya's plot failed, he fled to Yehhe, Butai was installed as chief, and the escorts returned.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月，布佔泰以女弟妻貝勒舒爾哈齊。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of winter Butai gave his younger sister in marriage to Beile Shuerhachi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of winter Butai gave his younger sister to Beile Shuerhachi in marriage.

sentences.zh: 二十五年春正月，與葉赫諸部同遣使請盟，盟甫罷，布佔泰旋執太祖所屬瓦爾喀部安褚拉庫所推者羅屯、噶石屯、汪吉努三人送葉赫，使招所部貳於太祖；

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the twenty-fifth year, together with the Yehhe tribes he sent envoys to request alliance; when the covenant had just ended, Butai seized Luotun, Gashitun, and Wangjinu—whom the Taizu's Waljir tribe of Anzhulaku had chosen—and sent them to Yehhe to entice that tribe's followers to defect from the Taizu;
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-fifth year he joined the Yehhe tribes in suing for peace; no sooner was the pact sealed than Butai seized Luotun, Gashitun, and Wangjinu—leaders chosen by the Taizu's Waljir followers in Anzhulaku—and sent them to Yehhe to turn those people against the Taizu;

sentences.zh: 又以滿、

translations.literal: He also sent Nalinbulu the copper hammer treasured by Mantai's wife Duduhu.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Nalinbulu the copper hammer that Mantai's wife Duduhu treasured.

sentences.zh: 內河二路頭人為泰妻都都祜所寶銅錘？

translations.literal: and the chiefs of the two inner-river routes, Wei Tai, and Mantai's wife Duduhu's treasured copper hammer, to Nalinbulu.
translations.idiomatic: and the inner-river two-route chiefs Wei Tai, together with the copper hammer that Mantai's wife Duduhu treasured, to Nalinbulu.

sentences.zh: 納林布祿。

translations.literal: Nalinbulu.
translations.idiomatic: to Yehhe Beile Nalinbulu.

sentences.zh: 二十六年春正月，太祖命台吉褚英等伐安褚拉庫路。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the twenty-sixth year, the Taizu ordered Taiji Chuying and others to campaign against the Anzhulaku route.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring in the twenty-sixth year, the Taizu sent Taiji Chuying and others to attack the Anzhulaku district.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月，布佔泰來謁，以三百人俱，太祖以舒爾哈齊女妻之，賜甲胄五十，敕書十道，禮而遣之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of winter, Butantai came to audience, with three hundred men in company; the Taizu gave him Shuerhachi's daughter in marriage, bestowed fifty suits of armor, ten patent letters of appointment, treated him with ceremony, and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of winter Butantai came to pay his respects, accompanied by three hundred men. The Taizu married him to a daughter of Shuerhachi, gave him fifty suits of armor and ten imperial patents, received him with full ceremony, and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 二十九年冬十一月乙未朔，布佔泰以其兄滿泰女歸太祖。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eleventh month of winter in the twenty-ninth year, the day yimao, Butantai sent his elder brother Mantai's daughter to the Taizu in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eleventh month of winter in the twenty-ninth year (yimao), Butantai sent his brother Mantai's daughter to the Taizu as a bride.

sentences.zh: 布佔泰初聘布寨女，既又聘明安女，以鎧冑、貂、猞猁猻裘、金銀、駝馬為聘，明安受之而不予女。

translations.literal: Butantai at first betrothed a daughter of Buzhai, then again betrothed a daughter of Ming'an, offering armor, sable, lynx-fur coats, gold and silver, and camels and horses as bride-price; Ming'an accepted them but would not give the girl.
translations.idiomatic: Butantai had first sought Buzhai's daughter in marriage, then sought Ming'an's daughter, sending armor, sable, lynx pelts, gold and silver, and camels and horses as betrothal gifts. Ming'an took the gifts but refused the girl.

sentences.zh: 三十一年春正月，布佔泰使告太祖曰：「我昔被擒，待以不死，俾我主烏喇，又妻我以公主，恩我甚深。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the thirty-first year, Butantai sent to tell the Taizu, saying: 'I was once captured; you spared my life, made me lord of Wula, and moreover gave me a princess in marriage—your grace to me was very deep.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring in the thirty-first year Butantai sent word to the Taizu: 'When I was taken prisoner you spared me, restored me to rule Wula, and gave me a princess in marriage. Your kindness was profound.

sentences.zh: 我孤恩，嘗聘葉赫、蒙古女，未敢以告。

translations.literal: I was ungrateful and once betrothed women of Yehhe and the Mongols, not daring to tell you.
translations.idiomatic: I betrayed that grace: I once sought brides from Yehhe and from the Mongols, but did not dare tell you.

sentences.zh: 今蒙古受聘而復悔，我甚恥之！

translations.literal: Now the Mongols have taken the bride-price and yet repent of the match—I am deeply shamed by it!
translations.idiomatic: Now the Mongols have taken my gifts and broken the betrothal. I am ashamed beyond measure!

sentences.zh: 乞再降以女，當歲歲從兩公主來朝。」

translations.literal: I beg that you again send down a daughter to me; each year I shall come to court with both princesses.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to give me another daughter in marriage. Every year I shall come to court with both your princesses.'

sentences.zh: 太祖允其請，又以舒爾哈齊女妻焉。

translations.literal: The Taizu granted his request and again gave him a daughter of Shuerhachi in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu granted his request and again married him to a daughter of Shuerhachi.

sentences.zh: 三十五年春正月，東海瓦爾喀部蜚悠城長策穆特黑謁太祖，自陳屬烏喇，為布佔泰所虐，乞移家來附。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the thirty-fifth year, Chemuhei, chief of Feiyoucheng in the eastern-sea Waljir tribe, came to audience with the Taizu and declared himself subject to Wula but abused by Butantai, begging to move his household and come over in allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring in the thirty-fifth year Chemuhei, chief of Feiyoucheng in the eastern Waljir lands, came before the Taizu. He said he belonged to Wula but had been mistreated by Butantai, and begged permission to move his people and submit.

sentences.zh: 太祖命貝勒舒爾哈齊、褚英、代善率諸將費英東、扈爾漢、揚古利等以兵三千至蜚悠城，收環城屯寨五百戶，分兵三百授扈爾漢、揚古利護之先行。

translations.literal: The Taizu ordered Beile Shuerhachi, Chuying, and Daishan to lead the generals Feiyingdong, Hurhan, and Yangguli and others with three thousand troops to Feiyoucheng, gathered five hundred households of stockaded settlements around the city, and detached three hundred men, assigning Hurhan and Yangguli to escort them ahead.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu ordered Beiles Shuerhachi, Chuying, and Daishan, with the generals Feiyingdong, Hurhan, Yangguli, and others, to march three thousand men to Feiyoucheng. They collected five hundred households from the surrounding stockades and sent three hundred troops ahead under Hurhan and Yangguli as escort.

sentences.zh: 布佔泰使其叔博克多將萬人要諸途。

translations.literal: Butantai sent his uncle Bokeduo to lead ten thousand men to block the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Butantai sent his uncle Bokeduo with ten thousand men to intercept them on the march.

sentences.zh: 日暮，扈爾漢依山結寨以相持。

translations.literal: At day's end Hurhan built a stockade against the hills to hold his ground.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk Hurhan pitched a camp against the hillside and held his position.

sentences.zh: 翌日，烏喇兵來攻，揚古利率兵擊敗之，烏喇兵引退，渡河陟山為固。

translations.literal: The next day Wula troops came to attack; Yangguli led troops and defeated them; the Wula army withdrew, crossed the river, and climbed the hills to make a stand.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Wula forces attacked. Yangguli drove them back. The Wula troops retreated across the river and fortified themselves on the heights.

sentences.zh: 褚英、代善等率後軍至，緣山奮擊，烏喇兵大敗，代善陣斬，俘其將常住、胡里布等，斬三千級，獲馬？

translations.literal: Chuying, Daishan, and others led the rear army up; striking fiercely along the hills, the Wula army was utterly defeated; Daishan slew enemies in the battle line, captured their generals Changzhu, Hulibu, and Bokeduo, beheaded three thousand, and seized three thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: Chuying and Daishan arrived with the rear guard and charged along the ridge. The Wula army was routed. Daishan killed many in the press of battle; they took the generals Changzhu and Hulibu prisoner, struck down three thousand heads, captured three thousand horses, and took Bokeduo.

sentences.zh: 博克多。

translations.literal: Bokeduo.
translations.idiomatic: and took Bokeduo prisoner.

sentences.zh: 是日晝晦，雪，甚寒，烏喇兵死者甚五千、甲三千以還。

translations.literal: That day the daylight was dim, snow fell, and it was very cold; Wula dead were very numerous; three thousand suits of armor were taken and they returned.
translations.idiomatic: That day the sky darkened, snow fell, and the cold was bitter. Wula dead numbered in the thousands; the victors brought back three thousand suits of armor.

sentences.zh: 三十六年春正月，太祖復命褚英及台吉阿敏將五千人伐烏喇，克宜罕阿麟城，斬千人。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the thirty-sixth year, the Taizu again ordered Chuying and Taiji Amin to lead five thousand men to campaign against Wula, took the city of Yihanalin, and beheaded a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring in the thirty-sixth year the Taizu again sent Chuying and Taiji Amin with five thousand men against Wula. They took Yihanalin city and slew a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 布佔泰糾蒙古科爾沁貝勒甕阿代，合軍屯所居城外二十里，畏褚，

translations.literal: Butantai rallied Mongol Khorchin Beile Weng'adai, joined armies, and encamped twenty li outside his dwelling, fearing Chuying and the others' strong army.
translations.idiomatic: Butantai called up the Mongol Khorchin beile Weng'adai, united their forces, and camped twenty li outside his stronghold, afraid of Chuying's strong army.

sentences.zh: 獲甲三百，俘其餘英等軍強，不敢進，引還。

translations.literal: and others' army was strong; they captured three hundred suits of armor but did not dare advance and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: and the others' army was too strong. They seized three hundred suits of armor, dared not press the attack, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，遣使復請修好，太祖使報問。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn he sent envoys again to request renewed peace; the Taizu sent a reply.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn he sent envoys to sue again for peace. The Taizu answered through his own messenger.

sentences.zh: 布佔泰執納林布祿所部種人五十輩，？

translations.literal: Butantai seized fifty of the tribesmen under Nalinbulu's command and sent them.
translations.idiomatic: Butantai seized fifty tribesmen who belonged to Nalinbulu's following and sent them on.

sentences.zh: 太祖使者盡殺之。

translations.literal: The Taizu's envoy had them all killed.
translations.idiomatic: and the Taizu's envoy had them all put to death.

sentences.zh: 又遣使來請曰：「我數背盟，獲罪於君父，若更以女子子妻我，撫我如子，我永賴以生矣。」

translations.literal: He again sent envoys to request, saying: 'I have repeatedly broken covenant and offended my lord and father; if you again give me a daughter in marriage and cherish me as a son, I shall forever rely on you to live.'
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys again with this plea: 'I have broken faith again and again and sinned against my lord. If you will give me another daughter and treat me as your own son, I shall live only by your grace.'

sentences.zh: 太祖复允其請，又以女子子妻之。

translations.literal: The Taizu again granted his request and again gave him a daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu granted his request once more and gave him another daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 四十年，布佔泰复背盟，秋九月，侵太祖所屬虎爾哈路，复欲娶太祖所聘葉赫貝勒布寨女，又以鳴鏑射所娶太祖女。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year Butantai again broke covenant; in the ninth month of autumn he invaded the Taizu's subject territory on the Hurha route, again wished to marry the daughter of Yehhe Beile Buzhai whom the Taizu had betrothed, and moreover shot whistling arrows at the Taizu's daughter whom he had married.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year Butantai broke faith again. In the ninth month of autumn he raided the Taizu's Hurha districts, sought to marry the daughter of Yehhe beile Buzhai—already promised to the Taizu—and even shot signal arrows at the Taizu's own daughter, his wife.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之怒，癸丑，親率兵伐之。

translations.literal: The Taizu heard and was angry; on the day guichou he personally led troops to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taizu heard this he was furious. On guichou day he led the army in person against Wula.

sentences.zh: 庚申，兵臨烏喇河，布佔泰以所部迎戰，夾河見太祖軍甲胄甚具，士馬盛強，烏喇兵人人惴恐，不敢渡。

translations.literal: On the day gengshen the army reached the Wula River; Butantai met the attack with his following; across the river they saw the Taizu's army's armor very complete and men and horses abundant and strong; every Wula soldier was fearful and did not dare cross.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day the army reached the Wula River. Butantai came out with his troops. From across the river his men saw the Taizu's armor glittering and his host in full strength. The Wula soldiers were afraid, and none dared cross.

sentences.zh: 太祖循河行，下河濱屬城五，又取金州城，遂駐軍焉。

translations.literal: The Taizu marched along the river, reduced five subject cities along the riverbank, also took Jinzhou city, and then encamped there.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu marched along the river, took five towns on the near bank, then captured Jinzhou and made camp there.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月辛酉朔，太祖以太牢告天祭纛，青白氣見東方，指烏喇城北。

translations.literal: On the first day of the twelfth month of winter, the day xinyou, the Taizu offered the great sacrifice to Heaven and performed the banner rite; azure-white vapors appeared in the east, pointing toward the north of Wula city.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the twelfth month of winter (xinyou) the Taizu sacrificed to Heaven with the grand offering and raised the war banner. Pale green and white vapors rose in the east, stretching toward the north of Wula.

sentences.zh: 太祖屯其地三日，盡焚其儲峙。

translations.literal: The Taizu encamped in that place three days and burned all their stored provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu camped there three days and burned every storehouse and granary.

sentences.zh: 布佔泰晝引兵出城，暮入城休。

translations.literal: Butantai by day led troops out of the city and by evening entered the city to rest.
translations.idiomatic: By day Butantai led his men out; each evening he withdrew into the city.

sentences.zh: 太祖率兵毀所下六城，廬舍、糗糧皆燼，移軍駐伏爾哈河渡口。

translations.literal: The Taizu led troops to destroy the six cities he had taken; lodges and grain stores were all burned to ash; he moved the army to encamp at the Volha River crossing.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu destroyed the six towns he had seized, burning dwellings and provisions alike, then shifted camp to the Volha River ford.

sentences.zh: 布佔泰使使者三輩以舟出見太祖，布佔泰率其弟喀爾喀瑪及所部拉布泰等繼以舟出，？

translations.literal: Butantai sent three envoys in boats to come out and see the Taizu; Butantai led his younger brother K'erhk'ema and his follower Labutai and others to follow in boats and come out.
translations.idiomatic: Butantai sent three envoys out in boats to meet the Taizu. He himself followed with his brother K'erhk'ema, Labutai, and others, also coming out by boat.

sentences.zh: 舟中而言曰：「烏喇國即父國也，幸毋盡焚我廬舍、糗糧。」

translations.literal: Speaking from the boat he said: 'The state of Wula is your father-state; I beg you not to burn all my lodges and grain stores.
translations.idiomatic: From the boat he cried: 'Wula is your father's house. I beg you—do not burn all my homes and stores.'

sentences.zh: 叩首請甚哀。

translations.literal: He kowtowed and pleaded very piteously.
translations.idiomatic: He kowtowed again and again, pleading in grief.

sentences.zh: 太祖立馬河中，數其罪。

translations.literal: The Taizu stood his horse in the midst of the river and recounted his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu sat his horse in midstream and listed his crimes.

sentences.zh: 布佔泰對曰：「此特讒者離間，使我父子不睦。

translations.literal: Butantai replied, saying: 'This is only slanderers driving us apart, making father and son estranged.
translations.idiomatic: Butantai answered: 'Slanderers have set us at odds and made father and son enemies.

sentences.zh: 我今在舟中，若果有此，惟天惟河神其共鑑之！」

translations.literal: I am now in this boat; if it were truly so, may Heaven and the river god together witness it!'
translations.idiomatic: I stand in this boat. If I have done what you say, let Heaven and the river god bear witness!'

sentences.zh: 拉布泰自旁儳曰：「貝勒既以此怒，曷不以使者來詰？」

translations.literal: Labutai from the side interrupted, saying: 'Since the beile is angry over this, why not send an envoy to question us?
translations.idiomatic: Labutai broke in from the side: 'If the beile is angry, why not send an envoy to demand an answer?'

sentences.zh: 太祖責之曰：「我部下豈少汝輩人耶？

translations.literal: The Taizu rebuked him, saying: 'Are men of your sort few in my following?
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu rebuked him: 'Do I lack men like you in my service?

sentences.zh: 事實矣，又何詰？

translations.literal: The facts are established—why question further?
translations.idiomatic: The facts are plain. What is there to question?

sentences.zh: 河冰無時，我兵來亦無時。

translations.literal: The river ice has no fixed season; my troops come likewise without fixed season.
translations.idiomatic: The river freezes when it will; my armies march when they will.

sentences.zh: 汝口雖利，能齒我刃乎？」

translations.literal: Your mouth may be sharp—can it bite my blade?'
translations.idiomatic: Your tongue is sharp—but can it turn my blade?'

sentences.zh: 布佔泰大懼，止拉布泰毋言。

translations.literal: Butantai was greatly afraid and stopped Labutai from speaking.
translations.idiomatic: Butantai was terrified and silenced Labutai.

sentences.zh: 喀爾喀瑪為乞宥，太祖乃命質其子及所部大酋子，遂還營。

translations.literal: K'erhk'ema pleaded for pardon; the Taizu then ordered hostages of his sons and the sons of great chiefs of his following, and then returned to camp.
translations.idiomatic: K'erhk'ema begged for mercy. The Taizu demanded hostages—Butantai's sons and the sons of his great chiefs—then withdrew to camp.

sentences.zh: 五日引還，度烏喇河濱邑麻虎山巔，以木為城，留千人戍焉。

translations.literal: After five days he led the army back, crossed to the peak of Mahu Mountain on the Wula River bank, built a palisade city of timber, and left a thousand men to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Five days later he marched home. On Mahu Mountain above the Wula he built a wooden fort and left a thousand men to hold it.

sentences.zh: 十二月，有白氣起烏喇，經太祖所居南屬虎攔哈達山。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month a white vapor rose from Wula, passing the Taizu's dwelling southward along Hulan Hada Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month a white comet rose over Wula and swept past the Taizu's camp southward along Hulan Hada ridge.

sentences.zh: 布佔泰旋复背盟，幽太祖及舒爾哈齊女，將以其女薩哈廉子綽啟鼐及所部大酋子十七人質於葉赫，娶太祖所聘貝勒布寨女。

translations.literal: Butantai soon again broke covenant, imprisoned the Taizu's and Shuerhachi's daughters, was about to send his daughter, Sahalian's son Chuochinai, and seventeen sons of great chiefs of his following as hostages to Yehhe, and marry the daughter of Beile Buzhai whom the Taizu had betrothed.
translations.idiomatic: Butantai soon broke faith again. He shut up the Taizu's daughter and Shuerhachi's daughter, prepared to send his own daughter, his grandson Chuochinai, and seventeen sons of his chiefs as hostages to Yehhe, and to marry the girl already promised to the Taizu—Buzhai's daughter.

sentences.zh: 四十一年春正月，太祖聞，复率兵伐之。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the forty-first year the Taizu heard and again personally led troops to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring in the forty-first year the Taizu heard the news and marched against Wula once more.

sentences.zh: 布佔泰期以是月丙子送其子出質，而太祖軍以乙亥至，攻下孫扎泰及郭多、俄謨三城。

translations.literal: Butantai had set the day bingzi of that month to send out his son as hostage, but the Taizu's army arrived on yihai and took the three cities Sunzhatai, Guoduo, and Emo.
translations.idiomatic: Butantai had promised to send his son out as hostage on bingzi day that month, but the Taizu's army arrived on yihai and seized the three towns Sunzhatai, Guoduo, and Emo.

sentences.zh: 丙子，布佔泰以兵三萬越伏爾哈城而軍，太祖猶欲諭之降。

translations.literal: On bingzi Butantai with thirty thousand troops crossed beyond Volha city and encamped; the Taizu still wished to instruct him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day Butantai brought thirty thousand men across Volha and drew up his line. The Taizu still hoped to persuade him to yield.

sentences.zh: 諸貝勒代善、阿敏，諸將費英東、何和里、扈爾漢、額亦都、安費揚古皆請戰，曰：「我利速戰，但慮彼不出耳。

translations.literal: The beiles Daishan and Amin, and the generals Feiyingdong, Heheli, Hurhan, Eidu, and Anfeyanggu all requested battle, saying: 'We profit from swift fighting—we only feared they would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Beiles Daishan and Amin, with the generals Feiyingdong, Heheli, Hurhan, Eidu, and Anfeyanggu, all pressed for battle: 'We gain by a quick fight—we only feared they would not come out.

sentences.zh: 今既出，平原廣野，可一鼓擒也！

translations.literal: Now that they have come out, on level plain and broad field we can take them at one drumbeat!
translations.idiomatic: Now they are in the open on level ground—we can break them in a single charge!

sentences.zh: 捨此不戰，厲兵秣馬，何為乎來？

translations.literal: To set this aside and not fight—sharpening weapons and feeding horses—why did we come?
translations.idiomatic: If we refuse battle after sharpening blades and feeding horses, why did we march here at all?

sentences.zh: 且使布佔泰娶葉赫女，辱莫甚焉！

translations.literal: Moreover, to let Butantai marry a Yehhe woman—no disgrace could be greater!
translations.idiomatic: And if we let Butantai marry the Yehhe girl—the insult could not be worse!

sentences.zh: 雖後討之，何益？」

translations.literal: Even if we punish him later, what use?
translations.idiomatic: Even if we punish him later, what good will it do?'

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「我荷天寵，自少在兵間，遇勁敵，無不單騎突陣者！

translations.literal: The Taizu said: 'I have received Heaven's favor; from youth in the midst of armies, meeting fierce enemies, there was none I did not charge the line alone!
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu said: 'Heaven has favored me. Since my youth, in every battle against a strong foe, I have ridden alone into the enemy line!

sentences.zh: 今日何難率汝輩身先搏戰。

translations.literal: Today what difficulty is there in leading you to fight hand to hand in the van?
translations.idiomatic: What difficulty is there today in leading you into the press ahead of all?

sentences.zh: 但慮諸貝勒、諸將或一二夷傷，我所深惜，故欲出萬全，非有所懼也。

translations.literal: But I fear that among the beiles and generals one or two might suffer wound or death—that I deeply regret—therefore I wished to secure complete safety; it is not that I have fear.
translations.idiomatic: But I dread that one of you beiles or generals might be wounded or killed. That is what I cannot bear. I sought a sure victory—not from fear.

sentences.zh: 今汝輩志一，即可決戰。」

translations.literal: Now your wills are one—you may decide the battle.
translations.idiomatic: Now your minds are one. Let us fight.'

sentences.zh: 因命被甲，諸貝勒、諸將則大歡，一軍盡甲，令曰：「勝即奪門，毋使復入！」

translations.literal: He then ordered armor donned; the beiles and generals rejoiced greatly; the whole army armored; the order was: 'On victory seize the gates—do not let them re-enter!'
translations.idiomatic: He ordered them to arm. The beiles and generals shouted for joy; the whole army buckled on armor. His command ran: 'When we win, take the gates—do not let them back inside!'

sentences.zh: 乃率兵進。

translations.literal: Then he led the army forward.
translations.idiomatic: Then he led the attack.

sentences.zh: 布佔泰自伏爾哈城率兵還，令其軍皆步為陣，兩軍距百步。

translations.literal: Butantai led troops back from Volha city, ordered his army all to fight on foot in formation; the two armies were a hundred paces apart.
translations.idiomatic: Butantai marched back from Volha and formed his men on foot. The two hosts stood a hundred paces apart.

sentences.zh: 太祖軍亦皆舍馬步戰，矢交如雨，呼聲震天。

translations.literal: The Taizu's army also all left their horses and fought on foot; arrows crossed like rain; shouts shook heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu's men too dismounted to fight. Arrows fell like rain; the battle cry shook the sky.

sentences.zh: 太祖躬入陣，諸貝勒、諸將從之縱擊，烏喇兵大敗，死者十六七。

translations.literal: The Taizu himself entered the formation; the beiles and generals followed him in fierce attack; the Wula army was utterly defeated; the dead were six or seven in ten.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu plunged into the fight himself. The beiles and generals followed in a furious charge. The Wula army broke; six or seven men in ten were slain.

sentences.zh: 師入，太祖坐西門樓，命樹幟。

translations.literal: The army entered; the Taizu sat on the western gate tower and ordered banners raised.
translations.idiomatic: The army entered the city. The Taizu took his seat on the western gate tower and ordered his banners raised.

sentences.zh: 布佔泰餘兵不滿百，還至城下，見幟則大奔。

translations.literal: Butantai's remaining troops were fewer than a hundred; returning to below the wall, they saw the banners and fled in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Butantai's remnant—fewer than a hundred men—reached the walls, saw the banners, and fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 遇代善，布佔泰兵皆潰，僅以身免，奔葉赫。

translations.literal: They met Daishan; Butantai's troops all collapsed; he alone escaped with his body and fled to Yehhe.
translations.idiomatic: They ran into Daishan. Butantai's force dissolved. He alone escaped and fled to Yehhe.

sentences.zh: 太祖使請於葉赫，葉赫不聽。

translations.literal: The Taizu sent to request him from Yehhe; Yehhe would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu demanded his surrender from Yehhe. Yehhe refused.

sentences.zh: 後七年，太祖克葉赫，布佔泰蓋已前死。

translations.literal: Seven years later the Taizu conquered Yehhe; Butantai had probably already died before that.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years later, when the Taizu overthrew Yehhe, Butantai was already dead.

sentences.zh: 拜音達里，輝發部長也。

translations.literal: Bayindari was chief of the Huifa tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Bayindari was chief of the Huifa tribe.

sentences.zh: 輝發亦扈倫四部之一，其先姓益克得里氏，居黑龍江岸。

translations.literal: Huifa was also one of the four Hulun tribes; their ancestors bore the surname Yikederi and dwelt on the Amur River bank.
translations.idiomatic: Huifa was one of the four Hulun tribes. Their forebears were of the Yikederi clan and lived on the banks of the Amur.

sentences.zh: 尼馬察部有昂古里星古力者，自黑龍江載木主遷於渣魯，居焉。

translations.literal: Among the Niman tribe was Angulixingguli, who from the Amur carried a wooden spirit tablet and moved to Zhalu, dwelling there.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Niman people was Angulixingguli, who carried his ancestral tablet down from the Amur and settled at Zhalu.

sentences.zh: 時扈倫部噶揚噶、圖墨土二人居張城，二人者姓納喇氏，昂古里星古力因附其族，宰七牛祭天，改姓納喇，是為輝發始祖。

translations.literal: At that time Gayangga and Tumu'tu of the Hulun tribe dwelt at Zhangcheng; the two were of the Nara clan; Angulixingguli therefore attached himself to their lineage, slaughtered seven oxen to sacrifice to Heaven, changed his surname to Nara—he was the founding ancestor of Huifa.
translations.idiomatic: Two men of the Nara clan, Gayangga and Tumu'tu of Hulun, then held Zhangcheng. Angulixingguli joined their line, sacrificed seven oxen to Heaven, and took the name Nara. He became the ancestor of Huifa.

sentences.zh: 昂古里星古力子二：留臣、備臣。

translations.literal: Angulixingguli had two sons: Liuchen and Beichen.
translations.idiomatic: Angulixingguli had two sons: Liuchen and Beichen.

sentences.zh: 備臣子二：納領噶、耐寬。

translations.literal: Beichen had two sons: Nalingga and Naikuan.
translations.idiomatic: Beichen had two sons: Nalingga and Naikuan.

sentences.zh: 納領噶生拉哈都督，拉哈都督生噶哈禪都督，噶哈禪都督生齊訥根達爾漢，齊訥根達爾漢生王機褚。

translations.literal: Nalingga begot Laha dudu; Laha dudu begot Gahachan dudu; Gahachan dudu begot Qinegendaerhan; Qinegendaerhan begot Wangjichu.
translations.idiomatic: Nalingga was father to Commander Laha; Laha to Commander Gahachan; Gahachan to Qinegendaerhan; Qinegendaerhan to Wangjichu.

sentences.zh: 王機褚收鄰近諸部，度輝發河濱扈爾奇山，築城以居，因號輝發。

translations.literal: Wangjichu gathered neighboring tribes, crossed to Hurqi Mountain on the Huifa River bank, built a city to dwell in, and therefore took the name Huifa.
translations.idiomatic: Wangjichu absorbed the neighboring tribes, crossed to Hurqi Mountain on the Huifa River, and built a walled town there. His people took the name Huifa from that place.

sentences.zh: 城負險堅峻，蒙古察哈爾部扎薩克圖土門汗嘗自將攻之，不能克。

translations.literal: The city leaned on perilous steepness and was firm and high; the Mongol Chakhar Zasakhtu Tumen Khan once personally led an attack on it and could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: The town stood on formidable heights. Zasakhtu Tumen Khan of the Mongol Chakhar once led the assault in person and failed to take it.

sentences.zh: 王機褚死時，其長子前死，孫拜音達里，殺其叔七人，自立為貝勒。

translations.literal: When Wangjichu died his eldest son had died earlier; the grandson Bayindari killed seven of his uncles and installed himself as beile.
translations.idiomatic: When Wangjichu died his eldest son was already dead. The grandson Bayindari killed seven uncles and made himself beile.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二十一年夏六月，葉赫糾哈達、烏喇諸部侵太祖，拜音達里以所部從。
