translations.literal: In the sixth month of summer in the twenty-first year of Wanli, Yehhe rallied Hada and Wula tribes to invade the Taizu; Bayindari followed with his following.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer in Wanli 21 Yehhe called up Hada and Wula against the Taizu. Bayindari marched with his tribe.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，复舉兵，拜音達里與哈達貝勒孟格布祿、烏喇貝勒布佔泰合兵萬人，兵敗，還。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn they again raised troops; Bayindari with Hada Beile Menggebulu and Wula Beile Butantai united armies of ten thousand men, were defeated, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month they attacked again. Bayindari joined Hada beile Menggebulu and Wula beile Butantai with ten thousand men. They were beaten and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 二十三年夏六月，太祖攻輝發，取所屬多璧城，輝發將克充格、蘇猛格二人戍，殲焉。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of summer of the twenty-third year the Taizu attacked Huifa, took the subject city Duobi, and annihilated the Huifa generals Kechongge and Sumengge who garrisoned it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer in the twenty-third year the Taizu struck Huifa and took Duobi. He wiped out the garrison commanded by Kechongge and Sumengge.

sentences.zh: 二十五年春正月有攜心。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the twenty-fifth year there was divided loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring in the twenty-fifth year his followers' loyalty wavered.

sentences.zh: 拜音，

translations.literal: Bayindari
translations.idiomatic: Bayindari

sentences.zh: 與葉赫諸部同遣使行成於太祖。

translations.literal: together with the Yehhe tribes jointly sent envoys to make peace with the Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: joined the Yehhe tribes in sending envoys to sue for peace with the Taizu.

sentences.zh: 居數年，拜音達里之族有叛附葉赫者，部達里懼，以所屬七人之子質於太祖，太祖發兵千人助之鎮撫。

translations.literal: After several years some of Bayindari's clan rebelled and went over to Yehhe; Bayindari was afraid and sent the sons of seven men of his following as hostages to the Taizu; the Taizu dispatched a thousand troops to help him pacify and garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Some years later part of Bayindari's clan defected to Yehhe. Bayindari, afraid, sent the sons of seven chiefs as hostages to the Taizu. The Taizu sent a thousand men to help him hold his people.

sentences.zh: 葉赫貝勒納林布祿使告拜音達里曰：「爾以質子歸我，亦歸爾叛族。」

translations.literal: Yehhe Beile Nalinbulu sent to tell Bayindari, saying: 'If you return the hostages to me, I will also return your rebellious clansmen.'
translations.idiomatic: Yehhe beile Nalinbulu sent word to Bayindari: 'Give me back the hostages and I will return your defectors.'

sentences.zh: 拜音達里信之，​​乃曰：「吾其中立於滿洲、葉赫二國之間乎！」

translations.literal: Bayindari believed him and therefore said: 'Shall I stand neutral between the two states of Manchu and Yehhe!'
translations.idiomatic: Bayindari believed him and said, 'Then I shall stand between Manchu and Yehhe and owe neither side!'

sentences.zh: 遂取質子還，以其子質於納林布祿。

translations.literal: He then took back the hostages and sent his own son as hostage to Nalinbulu.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled the hostages and sent his own son to Nalinbulu instead.

sentences.zh: 納林布祿殊無意歸叛族，拜音達里以告太祖，且曰：「吾前者為納林布祿所誑，怙舊恩，敢請婚。」

translations.literal: Nalinbulu had absolutely no intention of returning the rebellious clansmen; Bayindari reported this to the Taizu and moreover said: 'I was formerly deceived by Nalinbulu; relying on old grace, I dare request marriage.'
translations.idiomatic: Nalinbulu never meant to return the defectors. Bayindari told the Taizu, 'Nalinbulu tricked me before. Trusting in your old kindness, I dare ask for a marriage alliance.'

sentences.zh: 太祖許之。

translations.literal: The Taizu granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu agreed.

sentences.zh: 既而拜音達里背約不娶，太祖使詰之曰：「汝昔助葉赫，再舉兵侵我。

translations.literal: Before long Bayindari broke the covenant and would not marry; the Taizu sent to question him, saying: 'You formerly aided Yehhe and twice raised troops to invade me.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Bayindari broke the betrothal. The Taizu sent to rebuke him: 'You once aided Yehhe and twice marched against me.

sentences.zh: 我既宥爾罪，复許爾婚。

translations.literal: I have already pardoned your crime and again granted you marriage.
translations.idiomatic: I pardoned you and promised you my daughter.

sentences.zh: 今背約不娶，何也？」

translations.literal: Now you break covenant and will not marry—why?'
translations.idiomatic: Now you break faith and refuse the match. Why?'

sentences.zh: 拜音達里詭對曰：「吾子質葉赫，須其歸，娶爾女，與爾合謀。」

translations.literal: Bayindari answered deceitfully, saying: 'My son is hostage in Yehhe; he must return; then I shall marry your daughter and plot with you together.'
translations.idiomatic: Bayindari answered evasively: 'My son is hostage in Yehhe. When he returns I will marry your daughter and join you in counsel.'

sentences.zh: 因築城三重自固。

translations.literal: He therefore built triple walls to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: He then ringed himself with three lines of fortification.

sentences.zh: 及其子自葉赫歸，太祖復遣使問，拜音達里倚城堅，度兵即至，足以守，遂負盟。

translations.literal: When his son returned from Yehhe, the Taizu again sent envoys to inquire; Bayindari relied on his city's strength, reckoned that troops would soon arrive and that he could hold out, and therefore broke the covenant.
translations.idiomatic: When his son returned from Yehhe, the Taizu sent envoys again. Bayindari trusted his walls, reckoned that relief would come in time, and broke faith.

sentences.zh: 三十五年秋九月丙申，長星出東方指輝發，八夕乃滅。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn of the thirty-fifth year, on the day bingshen, a long comet appeared in the east pointing toward Huifa and was extinguished after eight nights.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn in the thirty-fifth year, on a bingshen day, a long comet rose in the east toward Huifa and faded after eight nights.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，太祖率師討之。

translations.literal: On yihai the Taizu led troops to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day the Taizu marched against him.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，合圍，遂克之，殺拜音達里及其子，安集其民，帥師還。

translations.literal: On jiachen they closed the encirclement, took the city, killed Bayindari and his son, settled the people, and led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day they closed the ring, took the city, killed Bayindari and his son, pacified the people, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 輝發亡。

translations.literal: Huifa perished.
translations.idiomatic: Huifa was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 論曰：扈倫四部，哈達最強，葉赫稍後起，與相埒，烏喇、輝發差弱。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Of the four Hulun tribes, Hada was strongest; Yehhe rose somewhat later and was its equal; Wula and Huifa were rather weaker.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Among the four Hulun tribes Hada was strongest; Yehhe rose later and matched it; Wula and Huifa were weaker.

sentences.zh: 其通於明，皆，令於所部則曰「國」。

translations.literal: In their dealings with the Ming, all were accounted as beile, and among their followers they were called "states."
translations.idiomatic: In their relations with the Ming they were all counted as beile, and among their followers they ruled as "states."

sentences.zh: 太祖漸強盛，四部合攻之，兵敗縱散，以次覆滅。

translations.literal: As the Taizu gradually grew strong, the four tribes united to attack him; their armies were defeated and scattered, and they were destroyed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: As the Taizu grew strong, the four tribes joined against him, were defeated and scattered, and fell one by one.

sentences.zh: 太祖與？

translations.literal: The Taizu,
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu,

sentences.zh: 以所領四部皆有連，奪其地，殲其酋，顯庸其族裔。

translations.literal: because the four tribes he led all had kinship ties, seized their lands, destroyed their chiefs, and ennobled their clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: because the four tribes under him were all linked by marriage and kinship, seized their lands, destroyed their chiefs, and ennobled their clansmen.

sentences.zh: 疆埸之事不以婚媾逭，有時乃藉口以啟戎，自古則然，不足異也。

translations.literal: Frontier affairs are not escaped through marriage alliances; sometimes pretexts are taken to begin war—thus it has been since antiquity, and is not to be wondered at.
translations.idiomatic: Border affairs are not settled by marriage alone; sometimes war is begun under the cover of such ties. It has always been so, and is nothing strange.
